articles.title: Gut-Brain coherence: a new therapeutic strategy for stress-related tumor.
articles.abstract: Chronic psychological stress significantly exacerbates tumor initiation, progression, and metastasis through neuroendocrine dysregulation and tumor-associated immunosuppression. Beyond direct neural pathways, stress is increasingly recognized as a driver of gut microbiota dysbiosis, which triggers systemic or local metabolic reprogramming, and fosters a suppressive tumor immune microenvironment. Understanding the complex interplay between chronic stress and oncogenic process offers critical insights into the underlying mechanisms of cancer biology. The microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA), as the primary pathway connecting stress to tumorigenesis, represents a pivotal perspective for deciphering this link. Here, we introduce "gut-brain coherence", defined as a dynamic, synchronized homeostasis among the gut microbial ecosystem, neuroendocrine tone, and immune effector function. Based on this concept, we present a dual-direction framework including microbial interventions, behavioral modulation, and targeted pharmacological strategies to re-establish integrated functional equilibrium, offering a unified roadmap to improve survival and quality of life in stress-driven malignancies.

articles.title: SIRT1 Signaling in Alzheimer's Disease: Regulation of Mitochondrial Biogenesis and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is one of the leading causes of dementia worldwide. Its pathological features include Aβ deposition, Tau hyperphosphorylation, and impaired neuronal energy metabolism, accompanied by persistent oxidative stress. As a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent deacetylase, sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) is a central regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis. This review systematically examines the emerging roles of SIRT1 in regulating these pathological processes in AD, with a particular focus on its regulation of mitochondrial biogenesis. It also delineates the complex regulatory mechanisms governing SIRT1, including NAD+-metabolism-dependent regulation, protein interaction-dependent regulation, post-translational modifications such as ISGylation and nitrosylation, and non-coding RNA-mediated post-transcriptional regulation. In addition, the coordinated influence of upstream activators and downstream effectors is discussed. Impairment of SIRT1-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis may exacerbate neuronal energy deficits and oxidative stress in AD, thereby increasing susceptibility to neurodegeneration. This review further elucidates the molecular mechanisms underlying the SIRT1-mitochondrial biogenesis axis. By integrating upstream activating signals with downstream effectors, SIRT1 creates a permissive regulatory environment for peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α)-driven, mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM)-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis, thereby facilitating quality-controlled renewal of the mitochondrial network. In addition, this review discusses the potential value of dynamic biomarker monitoring following therapeutic targeting of the SIRT1 pathway and summarizes current challenges and future intervention strategies. Targeting SIRT1-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis may provide a promising avenue for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for AD.

articles.title: Nanomedicine for Alzheimer's Disease: A Stage-Matched Framework Integrating Pathological Network Modulation, Blood-Brain Barrier Delivery, and Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains one of the most difficult neurodegenerative disorders to treat. Therapeutic failure is driven mainly by two barriers: the multifactorial pathological network of AD and the limited access of most therapeutics to the brain imposed by the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Conventional symptomatic drugs and emerging antibody-based therapies provide clinical benefit, but they do not fully address the interacting processes involving amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, Tau pathology, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and synaptic impairment. In this review, we discuss nanomedicine as an integrated platform for AD intervention. We summarize the major pathological nodes that provide targets for nanomedicine-based therapy and discuss BBB structure and transport mechanisms. We then compare polymeric, inorganic, carbon-based, lipid-based, protein-based, nucleic acid-based, and biomimetic platforms in terms of delivery function, intrinsic bioactivity, pathological modulation, and translational risk. Assisted brain-delivery strategies are also discussed, including focused ultrasound-mediated BBB modulation and intranasal nose-to-brain delivery. We then review clinical-stage AD nanomedicine candidates and summarize the key barriers to their translation. This review integrates stage-dependent pathology, BBB transport, and nanoplatform properties. It proposes a stage-matched framework for preclinical, mild symptomatic, and moderate-severe AD. At each stage, the framework matches active pathological nodes with feasible BBB transport strategies, carrier features, and administration routes. It may guide the development of mechanistically defined, reproducible, and clinically testable nanomedicines.

articles.title: Anti-PEG antibodies in drug delivery: From origins to mitigation strategies.
articles.abstract: Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) is a cornerstone excipient in drug delivery, widely used to prolong circulation duration and improve the therapeutic efficacy of protein therapeutics and nanomedicines. However, both pre-existing and treatment-induced anti-PEG antibodies have been increasingly recognized during clinical applications, raising concerns regarding the safety, efficacy, and translational reliability of PEGylated therapeutics. In this review, we summarize the origins and prevalence of anti-PEG antibodies, critically evaluate current detection methodologies, and analyze antibody-PEG binding patterns and downstream biological effects, including complement activation, accelerated blood clearance, hypersensitivity reactions, and tissue-specific toxicities, while emphasizing the context-dependent impact of anti-PEG immunity on therapeutic efficacy. We also discuss the emerging strategies to mitigate anti-PEG-mediated risks and outline the key challenges and future directions. This integrated framework aims to facilitate functional interpretation of anti-PEG immunity and support the rational design and clinical translation of next-generation PEGylated drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Herbal bioactive compounds modulating ferroptosis and pyroptosis in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury: a systematic review of molecular basis, proposed crosstalk, and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) remains a major cause of neonatal mortality and disability despite therapeutic hypothermia. Ferroptosis and pyroptosis are implicated in HIBI. PURPOSE: To critically evaluate herbal bioactive compounds modulating ferroptosis- and pyroptosis-associated injury in neonatal HIBI. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review conducted and reported following PRISMA 2020. METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Eligible studies used in vivo neonatal HIBI models, tested chemically defined plant-derived compounds, reported ferroptosis-related markers or evidence of pyroptotic execution beyond inflammasome activation, and assessed neuroprotective outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE. RESULTS: Of 1441 records, 17 studies investigating 16 compounds met eligibility criteria. Nine examined ferroptosis and eight examined pyroptosis; glycyrrhizin was the only compound studied across both pathways, in separate studies. Included compounds spanned diverse structural classes and botanical sources. Studies reported reduced pathway-associated markers and improved brain-injury outcomes, but in vivo pathway dependency was demonstrated for only four compounds. No included study reported both ferroptosis-specific and pyroptosis-specific markers in the same neonatal HIBI model. Several risk-of-bias domains were predominantly rated unclear. CONCLUSION: Preclinical studies suggest that herbal bioactives can modulate ferroptosis- and pyroptosis-associated processes in neonatal HIBI and warrant further evaluation as multi-target candidates. However, no study tested whether a single compound modulates both pathways within the same model. Future studies should apply pathway-specific manipulation alongside assessment of the second pathway in the same model and address developmental-stage specificity, therapeutic timing, model variability, brain availability, formulation barriers, and other pharmacological considerations.

articles.title: Metabolic conversion of dioscin-diosgenin and their interactions with gut microbiota: recent advances.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: HMF plants are rich sources of steroidal saponins, and dioscin and diosgenin are the widely distributed and bioactive compounds. Despite their poor oral bioavailability, these saponins undergo extensive microbial transformation, yielding bioavailable metabolites with enhanced lipophilicity and pharmacological potential. Recent studies indicate that the interaction between diosgenin and the gut microbiota plays a crucial role in regulating metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine functions. Understanding this bidirectional relationship may provide a foundation for developing novel microbiota-targeted nutritional and therapeutic strategies. PURPOSE: The purpose of this review was to summarize current research progress on the biotransformation, biological functions, and health implications of diosgenin and its precursors. We elucidate how microbial metabolism modulates diosgenin activity and how diosgenin reshapes gut microbial composition and function to maintain intestinal homeostasis. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted using four major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CNKI, were searched from inception to January 2026. Key words used in the literature search were "diosgenin", "dioscin", "steroidal saponins", "gut microbiota", "homology of medicine and food", "β-glucosidase", "microbial transformation", "mucosal immunity", "metabolic and inflammatory disorders" and "gut brain axis". Keywords are linked with AND/OR. Chemical structure data and biotransformation pathways were confirmed through peer-reviewed sources and authoritative databases such as NIH and PubChem. RESULTS: Evidence indicates that intestinal microbial β-glucosidases catalyze the deglycosylation of dioscin into lipophilic aglycone diosgenin, thereby enhancing its membrane permeability and bioactivity. Diosgenin selectively enriches beneficial microbial populations and promotes the production of key microbial metabolites, including SCFAs and tryptophan-derived indoles. These microbial metabolites play pivotal roles in intestinal epithelial integrity and mucosal immune homeostasis. They modulate the Treg balance by activating key host signaling pathways. The primary receptors involved include GPRs, AHR, and PPARs. Preclinical studies strongly support the therapeutic potential of the microbiota-diosgenin axis in alleviating T2D, NAFLD, IBD, neuroinflammation, and age-related pathologies. CONCLUSION: This review highlights the gut microbiota as an important modulator of diosgenin bioavailability and biological activity, based largely on preclinical evidence. Differences in microbial composition and metabolic capacity may contribute to interindividual variability in host responses to diosgenin. In this context, we propose the concept of diosgenin metabotypes as a conceptual framework to describe microbiota-dependent differences in diosgenin metabolism, which may inform future microbiome-guided nutritional and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Modulatory effects of marine algae-derived natural products on nervous system.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The pathological changes in neurodegenerative diseases are complicated and involve oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, protein misfolding, and synaptic loss. Marine algae contain a wide range of diverse natural compounds, such as polysaccharides, phenolics, terpenoids, and pigments, some of which may help preserve neurons by targeting oxidative pathways, dampening inflammatory responses, and preventing toxic protein aggregation. PURPOSE: This review aims to recapitulate current advances on the regulatory roles of marine algae-derived natural products on nervous system. In addition, representative compounds are discussed, together with the relationship between their structures and neuroprotective properties. METHODS: To conduct this structured narrative review, we collected relevant literature obtained from PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar up to June 2026. Relevant studies on the effect of algal products on neuroprotection were selected and articles were searched using terms that covered marine algae, natural products, neurodegenerative diseases, and structure-activity relationship. RESULTS: Natural products found in marine algae may support neuronal protection through the modulation of redox balance, inflammatory signaling, and proteostasis. Their neuroprotective activities are closely associated with structural determinants, and are intrinsically shaped by characteristics like sulfation degree, molecular weight, hydroxyl groups, and conjugated systems. CONCLUSION: This article underscores the potential of these products for neuroprotective interventions, and further studies are warranted to clarify their bioavailability and clinical efficacy.

articles.title: Cuproptosis in chemically induced neurotoxicity: current evidence and a testable framework for psychostimulant-induced neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Cuproptosis is a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by disruption of lipoylated mitochondrial proteins, iron-sulfur cluster instability, and proteotoxic stress. This review examines whether this pathway contributes to chemically induced neurotoxicity and to psychostimulant-associated neuronal injury. Recent experimental studies have expanded the neurotoxic contexts in which copper-dependent injury has been investigated, including environmental nanomaterials, toxic metals, copper overload, and pharmacological agents. Across these models, the strongest evidence combines altered copper homeostasis with pathway-specific molecular changes and functional intervention, although complete demonstration of canonical cuproptosis remains inconsistent. In psychostimulant models, the evidence is substantially less developed. Methamphetamine has recently been associated with alterations in ATP7A/B, FDX1, and lipoylated DLAT, whereas cocaine and synthetic cathinones remain supported mainly by mitochondrial, redox, and proteostatic abnormalities. None of these psychostimulant models has yet established copper-dependent neuronal death through the complete canonical pathway. The current literature therefore supports cuproptosis as an emerging mechanism in selected forms of chemically induced neurotoxicity, while its role in psychostimulant injury remains a testable but unconfirmed hypothesis.

articles.title: Making hormesis visible in new approach methodologies (NAMs): a framework for botanical mixtures, biological context, and risk interpretation.
articles.abstract: Risk characterization of mixtures such as botanicals is complicated by their complex and variable composition, where there are multiple possibilities for interactions among components, even at low doses. Most traditional toxicological testing and risk-assessment workflows remain optimized for monotonic toxicity. New approach methodologies (NAMs) are much better able to detect low-concentration and time-dependent stimulation or inhibition in complex mixtures, which can vary across donors, sexes, biological states, and production lots. We propose H-NAM, a hormesis-aware overlay for existing NAM batteries and integrated approaches to testing and assessment. H-NAM uses the commonly reported 30-60% maximum stimulation and the often narrow, sub-decade stimulatory concentration window as empirical design heuristics rather than universal biological rules. It integrates two-stage concentration design, time-resolved measurements, relevant biological-context strata, botanical identity and multi-lot controls, assay-interference testing, comparison of monotonic, biphasic, and flexible response models, and quantitative in vitro-in vivo extrapolation. H-NAM separates four questions: (1) whether a biphasic response pattern is credible; (2) how it varies across concentration, time, and biological context; (3) whether the stimulation is adaptive, an early-warning signal, ambiguous, or adverse; and (4) whether the relevant response region is attainable under plausible internal exposure. Exposure relevance is evaluated independently using time-matched exposure estimates and an exploratory stimulatory bioactivity-exposure ratio (sBER). Joint evaluation of biological consequence and exposure relevance is then used to prioritize follow-up testing, hazard characterization, candidate point-of-departure development, or risk management, while a lot-restricted response prompts compositional and manufacturing investigation. H-NAM is intended to reduce both the dismissal of reproducible low-concentration signals and the unsupported interpretation of stimulation as benefit or evidence of safety. An accompanying reporting checklist is suggested for specifying the minimum information needed for independent evaluation, replication, and regulatory interpretation.

articles.title: T-2 toxin toxicity: what do we currently know about the most toxic trichothecene mycotoxin?
articles.abstract: T-2 toxin, a type A trichothecene mycotoxin produced by Fusarium species, is recognized as one of the most potent contaminants of cereals and cereal-based products worldwide. Despite decades of investigation, its toxicological profile continues to expand as new mechanistic insights emerge from molecular biology, omics technologies, and computational toxicology. This state-of-the-art review critically reassesses current knowledge regarding the physicochemical characteristics, environmental occurrence, exposure pathways, metabolism, and regulatory aspects of T-2 toxin, with particular emphasis on its mechanisms of action.T-2 induces pronounced e.g. oxidative stress, disrupts mitochondrial membrane potential, promotes cytochrome c release, and activates caspase-dependent apoptosis. Emerging evidence further implicates immunotoxic, neurotoxic, cardiotoxic, and nephrotoxic effects, as well as modulation of Nrf2, JAK/STAT, inflammasome, and autophagy-related pathways.The review integrates findings from in chemico, in vitro, in vivo, and New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including QSAR and in silico modeling approaches that support predictive toxicology and risk assessment. Special attention is given to metabolic transformation into other derivatives, scenarios with other Fusarium mycotoxins, and climate-driven changes in contamination patterns. Collectively, this multidimensional synthesis highlights persistent knowledge gaps and underscores the need for integrative, mechanism-based frameworks in future regulatory evaluation of T-2 toxin with in silico methods.

articles.title: Advancing Evidence Generation in Small, Diverse, Understudied Population.
articles.abstract: Many clinically important patient groups remain systematically underrepresented in drug development. Among these are patients with severe or time-varying organ dysfunction, pregnant and lactating women, children with ultrarare diseases, and people from socioeconomically or geographically underserved communities. Traditional clinical trials frequently exclude such groups. Little direct evidence is generated as a result, leaving benefit-risk and dosing decisions uncertain and trial findings poorly generalizable to the patients who will ultimately receive the drug. No single method closes this gap. This review argues that progress instead comes from integration, combining model-informed drug development, registries and real-world data, external and virtual controls, Bayesian borrowing, and patient-centric trial designs into a coherent totality-of-evidence package. These tools are maturing from a role that supplements clinical data toward one that can, in defined settings, partially replace it. The appropriate approach may differ by population. For example, (1) mechanistic modeling and exposure prediction for organ replacement therapy/changing organ function or from the altered maternal-fetal-infant physiology that makes prospective studies impractical; (2) registry-based external controls and natural history data where patients are too few to randomize; and (3) decentralized, partnership-driven designs to reach populations that structural barriers would otherwise exclude. Three case studies (dose justification across hepatic and renal impairment, evidence generation in women of childbearing potential with chronic autoimmune disease, and a registry-anchored ultrarare pediatric program) illustrated these approaches. Mapped to evolving regulatory frameworks, these strategies can deliver population-appropriate dosing at approval rather than through postmarketing commitments, accelerating equitable access to safe and effective therapies.

articles.title: PSMA Biology Through the Clinical Lens: Implications for Radioligand Therapy of Prostate Cancer with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in men worldwide. While hormone therapy is effective in the early stages of advanced disease, multimodal approaches are often required as disease progresses, including radiotherapy, hormonal agents and chemotherapy. In metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), tumour cells become resistant to hormone therapy, resulting in poor survival outcomes despite systemic treatments. Among emerging therapies, radioligand therapy targeting prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) has shown promise. PSMA is a transmembrane glycoprotein highly expressed in prostate cancer cells, with minimal expression in normal tissues. This selective distribution enables precision targeting and minimises toxicity. The radiotheranostic agent [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 combines PSMA-617, a small molecule ligand, with the beta-emitting radioisotope 177Lutetium. This therapy has demonstrated efficacy in patients with mCRPC who have progressed after androgen receptor pathway inhibitors and taxane-based chemotherapy. Its regulatory approval in the USA, UK and Europe marks a pivotal advancement in prostate cancer management. Clinical trials such as TheraP, VISION and PSMAfore have established the role of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 in mCRPC and its potential additive effects with other anti-tumour therapies are under investigation. Strategies to enhance PSMA expression may further improve therapeutic response. With no relevant drug-drug interaction risk, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 may be safely considered for use in combination with other therapies, a key advantage for frail patients with mCRPC on polypharmacy. Post-treatment management remains a challenge and ongoing research aims to optimise long-term outcomes. This review provides a comprehensive update on [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 therapy, from molecular mechanisms to clinical application and outlines future directions in the treatment of advanced prostate cancer.

articles.title: Targeting ACKR1+ Endothelial Cells Attenuates Pulmonary Fibrosis by Halting Monocytes Infiltration/Polarization and Endothelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition.
articles.abstract: While microvascular abnormalities drive idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), the pathogenic endothelial subpopulations and their specific molecular networks are poorly understood. By integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, we identified a pathologically expanded ACKR1+ endothelial cell (EC) subpopulation that correlates with pulmonary function decline and forms a pro-fibrotic endothelial-fibroblast niche in IPF. Within this niche, fibroblast-derived TGF-β upregulates endothelial ACKR1 transcription via the SMAD2 axis. We demonstrate that ACKR1+ ECs promote fibrosis through two distinct mechanisms. At the cellular level, interactome mapping shows ACKR1 drives endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) by competitively sequestering the endocytic adaptor NUMB, which prevents NOTCH1 lysosomal degradation and sustains Notch hyperactivation. In the microenvironment, ACKR1+ ECs mediate monocyte recruitment via CCL2 transcytosis and secrete IGFBP7, polarizing pro-fibrotic M2 macrophages through the CD93/PI3K/AKT signaling axis. Endothelial-specific deletion of Ackr1 protects against bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Through structure-based virtual screening, we identified 1F-Fructofuranosylnystose as a direct ACKR1 inhibitor. Pharmacological blockade with 1F-Fructofuranosylnystose halted EndMT and pathogenic macrophage recruitment, preserving lung architecture and respiratory mechanics in murine models, ferret models, and human precision-cut lung slices. These findings establish the mechanistic basis of ACKR1+ ECs in fibrosis and highlight ACKR1 inhibition as a targeted therapeutic approach for IPF.

articles.title: mRNA folding facilitates efficient and spleen-targeted delivery by highly branched poly(β-amino ester)s.
articles.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA)-based therapeutics hold great promise in preventing and treating various diseases. However, the instability and high immunogenicity of raw mRNA molecules, along with the inefficient delivery vectors, strictly limited the proteins translation and therapeutic applications. In this work, we successfully engineered a folded structural mRNA for enhancing its stability by leveraging a magnesium ion (Mg2+)-mediated charge neutralization and structural compression strategy. Further, a functionalized highly branched poly(β-amino ester)s (HPAEs) was utilized to efficiently deliver the folded mRNA, achieving specifically targeting to the spleen. Notably, compared with polyplexes containing non-folded mRNA, the optimal folded mRNA-based polyplexes exhibited stronger mRNA encapsulation, smaller size, and a more homogeneous morphology; ultimately, demonstrated higher mRNA transfection efficiency up to 85.4% across five different cell types, maintaining high cell viability. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that Mg2+-mediated mRNA folding strategy dramatically enhanced the folded mRNA-formulated polyplexes cellular uptake and endosomal escape. Encouragingly, when administered systemically, the representative folded mRNA-based polyplexes demonstrated robust protein expression, yielding 3-fold enhancement in spleen, compared to the unfolded mRNA-based nanoparticles, showing superior biosafety in vivo. Collectively, the work establishes a new class of the folded structure mRNA polymer delivery system, and provides a foundation for the next generation of RNA-based therapeutic drugs for spleen-related diseases.

articles.title: A zinc-sequestering polymer disrupts zinc homeostasis to suppress fungal viability and virulence.
articles.abstract: Zinc is a central structural cofactor in fungi, supporting transcriptional control and mitochondrial function, and its tightly regulated homeostasis presents an underexploited antifungal intervention point. Targeting zinc-dependent architectures offers a mechanistically distinct alternative to conventional membrane- or cell wall-directed antifungals. Here we report a zinc- deprivation fungicide (ZDF) by grafting high-affinity bipyridine chelators onto ε-poly-l-lysine, enabling intracellular sequestration of labile zinc without overt membrane disruption. ZDF-induced zinc depletion disrupts zinc-dependent RNA processing, particularly mitochondrial tRNA modification, thereby collapsing mitochondrial translation, impairing oxidative phosphorylation, and inducing profound energetic failure. ZDF further remodels zinc-dependent regulatory networks, downregulating drug efflux to restore azole-resistant strains and suppressing biofilm maturation via zinc-responsive Zap1-Dpp1-farnesol axis. This strategy shows high selectivity over mammalian cells, and outperforms clinical azoles in murine cutaneous wound and rabbit keratitis models. By employing the unique role of zinc as an essential structural cofactor for fungal transcriptional regulators, this work defines intracellular zinc sequestration as a non-membrane-directed antifungal strategy that exploits a central regulatory dependency in fungi.

articles.title: PKA-dependent phosphorylation of PSMG1 reduces bortezomib sensitivity in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: AIMS: This study aimed to characterize PSMG1 expression and its phosphorylation status in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and dissect its functional role in regulating bortezomib (BTZ) chemosensitivity. METHODS: Western blotting, Flag co-immunoprecipitation and GST pull-down assays were applied to profile protein abundance, protein-protein binding and phosphorylation signaling cascades. Flow cytometry quantified apoptotic cell populations. Fluorogenic peptide substrates were utilized to measure cellular chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity. MTT, colony formation and Transwell migration assays were performed to evaluate proliferative and migratory phenotypes. In vivo anti-tumor efficacy of BTZ monotherapy and BTZ/H89 co-treatment was validated in subcutaneous HCC xenograft mouse models. RESULTS: PSMG1 protein was aberrantly overexpressed in HCC tissues, and high PSMG1 abundance independently predicted dismal patient survival. Genetic ablation of PSMG1 suppressed chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity and sensitized HCC cells to BTZ, without altering intrinsic cell proliferation or migratory capacity. Protein kinase A (PKA) physically bound PSMG1 and was associated with its phosphorylation at residues T18 and T54. This post-translational modification was correlated with elevated chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity and reduced sensitivity of HCC cells to BTZ. Consistently, pharmacological blockade of PKA via H89 enhanced BTZ cytotoxicity in HCC. Immunohistochemical profiling revealed elevated PKA-pT197 levels in HCC lesions, which exhibited a modest positive correlation with PSMG1-pT18 phosphorylation signals. CONCLUSIONS: PKA activity is associated with PSMG1 phosphorylation, which may contribute to reduced BTZ sensitivity in HCC. Pharmacological inhibition of PKA with H89 enhanced bortezomib cytotoxicity in preclinical HCC models, providing a preliminary rationale for combination strategies to increase proteasome inhibitor sensitivity in HCC management.

articles.title: Eupalinolide B targets the USP10-AR-MTHFD1 axis to sensitize castration-resistant prostate cancer to enzalutamide.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acquired resistance to enzalutamide (ENZ) remains a major obstacle in the treatment of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Although persistent androgen receptor (AR) signaling is a central determinant of limited responsiveness to ENZ, the post-translational mechanisms that maintain AR protein stability during ENZ treatment remain insufficiently understood. PURPOSE: This study aimed to define the role of ubiquitin-specific protease 10 (USP10) in CRPC adaptive responses to ENZ treatment and determine whether Eupalinolide B (EB) could enhance ENZ sensitivity by targeting the USP10-AR-MTHFD1 axis. METHODS: CRPC cell models and xenograft mouse models were established to evaluate the effects of EB on ENZ sensitivity both in vitro and in vivo. Protein interaction and localization were analyzed using immunoprecipitation, binding assays and immunofluorescence. AR ubiquitination and degradation were evaluated by ubiquitination assays and proteasome inhibition experiments. Functional assays were performed to investigate the impact of EB on cell proliferation and tumor progression, and mechanistic studies were conducted to explore the involvement of the USP10-AR-MTHFD1 signaling axis. RESULTS: USP10 translocated to the nucleus under ENZ treatment and contributed to reduced ENZ responsiveness in CRPC. EB disrupted the USP10-AR interaction by targeting the catalytic domain of USP10, promoting ubiquitination-mediated AR degradation, and suppressing the downstream AR-MTHFD1 axis. Consequently, EB enhanced the antitumor efficacy of ENZ against CRPC both in vitro and in vivo. CONCLUSION: USP10 is a potential therapeutic vulnerability in CRPC, and EB represents a promising lead compound for ENZ-based combination therapy.

articles.title: Qishen Yangxin Granule ameliorates cardiac function and ventricular remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy by attenuating inflammation and myocardial fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Qishen Yangxin Granule (QSYX), a clinically utilized traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for cardiovascular diseases. However, its cardioprotective mechanism in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains incompletely defined. PURPOSE: To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of QSYX against DCM and the associated anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic mechanisms. METHODS: Cardioprotective effects of QSYX were assessed both in vivo using a doxorubicin-induced DCM rat model and in vitro using rat cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Evaluations included cardiac function, histopathological analysis, levels of inflammatory factors, and myocardial fibrosis markers. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to explore the potential mechanism of QSYX-mediated improvement in cardiac structure and function. Modulation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway was examined via western blot, immunohistochemistry, confocal laser scanning microscope, and real-time reverse transcription-PCR. The specific p38 MAPK agonist LY188011 was used to verify the dependence of QSYX effect on the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. RESULTS: QSYX administration improved cardiac function in DCM rats, accompanied by significant attenuation of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, apoptosis, inflammatory cell infiltration, and collagen deposition. Comparable protective effects were observed in lipopolysaccharide-treated cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, QSYX suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced upregulation of TLR4, p38 MAPK, and NF-κB p65 and downregulated the expression of inflammatory factors and myocardial fibrosis markers. Furthermore, intervention with LY188011 confirmed that the cardioprotective effects of QSYX are mediated through suppression of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: QSYX attenuates myocardial inflammation and fibrosis primarily through inhibition of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby exerting cardioprotective effects against DCM-induced cardiac injury.

articles.title: Jingfang granule alleviates cold-damp lung injury by suppressing NF-κB/HIF-1α-associated macrophage glycolysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Jingfang Granule (JFG) is clinically used for exterior cold-damp disorders, but its pulmonary effects and associated inflammatory responses remain incompletely understood. PURPOSE: To evaluate the protective effects of JFG against cold-damp syndrome-like lung injury and its effects on macrophage glycolytic inflammatory activation. STUDY DESIGN: A combined in vivo, multi-omics and in vitro mechanistic study was conducted. METHODS: Rats were exposed to low-temperature/high-humidity conditions and treated with JFG. Lung pathology, inflammatory responses, targeted serum energy metabolomics, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI), transcriptomics and proteomics were evaluated. UPLC fingerprinting and UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS-based serum pharmacochemistry were used to characterize JFG and its absorbed constituents. LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were treated with JFG-medicated serum. DMOG rescue, HIF-1α knockdown, BAY 11-7082-mediated NF-κB inhibition, fluorometric ECAR assay and representative-compound validation were performed to strengthen mechanistic interpretation. RESULTS: JFG improved cold-damp-related phenotypes, reduced pulmonary edema, mucus hypersecretion, inflammatory cytokine levels and CD68/iNOS-positive macrophage accumulation. Metabolomics and MALDI-MSI showed that JFG corrected glycolysis- and TCA cycle-related disturbances. Integrated multi-omics highlighted the NF-κB/HIF-1α-HK2/LDHA pathway as a major JFG-regulated axis. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, JFG-medicated serum reduced glycolysis-associated markers and CD86-positive M1-like activation. DMOG partially reversed these effects, whereas HIF-1α knockdown reduced HK2, LDHA, iNOS expression and extracellular acidification, weakening the additional inhibitory effect of JFG-medicated serum. BAY 11-7082 further supported the involvement of NF-κB in HIF-1α-associated glycolytic activation. Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin (POG), nobiletin and quercetin partially reproduced the inhibitory effects of JFG-medicated serum on pathway-associated proteins in vitro. CONCLUSION: JFG attenuated cold-damp syndrome-like lung injury in rats, accompanied by improvements in pulmonary inflammation and glycolysis-related metabolic disturbances. Complementary experiments in LPS-stimulated macrophages supported the involvement of NF-κB/HIF-1α-associated glycolytic activation in the anti-inflammatory effects of JFG-medicated serum, while serum pharmacochemistry provided evidence of absorbed constituents.

articles.title: Identification of cepharanthine as a novel senolytic that selectively eliminates senescent cells by regulating cell survival signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Senolytics are small-molecule drugs that selectively induce apoptosis in senescent cells, thereby reducing the chronic inflammation and tissue damage caused by the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and delaying aging, improving organ function and extending healthspan. Existing senolytics, however, often suffer from low bioavailability and off-target toxicity, so potent and safer senolytics are urgently needed. PURPOSE: To screen for novel senolytic compounds and validate the ability of cepharanthine (CEP) to eliminate senescent cells, improve organ function and extend lifespan. STUDY DESIGN: Preclinical study combining in vitro phenotypic screening and mechanistic assays with in vivo validation in zebrafish, C. elegans, naturally aged mice and a Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) mouse model. METHODS: Senolytic efficacy was assessed by a senescent cell-based phenotypic screen, IC₅₀ determination, inhibitor-based rescue assays and multiple senescence models. RNA-seq and pathway enrichment identified the key PI3K/AKT and PERK-ATF4-CHOP pathways, verified by Western blot, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence and mitochondrial assays. In vivo efficacy was evaluated by senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining, HE staining, immunofluorescence, ELISA, biochemical assays and survival analysis. RESULTS: CEP selectively eliminates senescent cells by cooperatively and in parallel regulating the PI3K/AKT and PERK-ATF4-CHOP pathways, differentially inducing PUMA/NOXA and triggering mitochondrial intrinsic apoptosis. In zebrafish, C. elegans, naturally aged mice and HGPS mice, CEP clears senescent cells, reduces SASP levels, improves organ function and prolongs lifespan. CONCLUSION: CEP is a novel natural senolytic that induces mitochondrial intrinsic apoptosis via parallel, non-redundant regulation of the PI3K/AKT and PERK-ATF4-CHOP pathways, showing good potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: A multifunctional Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide hydrogel loaded with propolis extract to promote oral mucosal repair.
articles.abstract: Oral ulcer is a prevalent mucosal injury characterized by bacterial infection, oxidative stress, and dysregulated inflammation, while current therapies remain insufficient to comprehensively regulate the complex healing process. Herein, we developed a multifunctional bioactive hydrogel (DH@Pro) by incorporating propolis extract into a dynamic polysaccharide network composed of Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide and phenylboronic acid-grafted hyaluronic acid HA-PBA. The DH@Pro hydrogel exhibited excellent antioxidant, immunomodulatory, regenerative properties and promoted angiogenesis. In vivo studies using rat oral ulcer models demonstrated that DH@Pro exerted distinct effects throughout different healing phases to achieve comprehensive oral ulcer repair. Furthermore, its therapeutic efficacy in a full-thickness skin wound model highlighted its broader regenerative potential. This study presents a natural polysaccharide-based hydrogel strategy that integrates infection control, inflammation regulation, and regeneration promotion for comprehensive oral ulcer repair.

articles.title: Adjunctive fucoidan, fucoxanthin, and l-carnitine mitigate albuminuria and preserve eGFR over a 12-week treatment period in diabetic kidney disease: A translational study and proof-of-concept randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Standard therapies for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) reduce albuminuria but trigger an acute eGFR decline, limiting clinical initiation. We evaluated whether a standardized marine formula comprising oligo-fucoidan, fucoxanthin, and l-carnitine (FFL) provides potential renoprotective effects with stable renal function. METHODS: Preclinically, diabetic CKD mice received FFL for 8 weeks. Clinically, a 12-week randomized trial evaluated adjunctive FFL in DKD patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors (100%) and ACEIs/ARBs (85.5%). Efficacy was analyzed using baseline-adjusted robust ANCOVA (per-protocol, n = 55) and validated under intention-to-treat (ITT, n = 63) sensitivity analysis with Baseline Observation Carried Forward imputation. RESULTS: Preclinically, FFL significantly attenuated renal dysfunction, tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and inflammation. Clinically, baseline-adjusted robust ANCOVA showed that adjunctive FFL achieved a highly significant, adjusted 39.40% greater reduction in UACR compared to control (Geometric Mean Ratio [GMR] = 0.60; 95% CI: 0.40-0.90; p = 0.01), which was validated under ITT-ANCOVA sensitivity analysis (adjusted 32.18% greater UACR reduction; GMR = 0.67; 95% CI: 0.48-0.93; p = 0.01). Crucially, eGFR remained stable and preserved over 12 weeks (PP adjusted GMR = 1.01, p = 0.74; ITT adjusted GMR = 1.01, p = 0.78). FFL also significantly lowered baseline-adjusted LDL (GMR = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95; p < 0.01) with a baseline-dependent response maximizing at a 24.28% reduction in patients with baseline dyslipidemia (p < 0.01), while displaying preliminary, exploratory glycemic signals. No serious adverse events or significant potassium elevations occurred. CONCLUSION: Standardized marine FFL is a safe, well-tolerated adjunctive therapy that reduces albuminuria and dyslipidemia while preserving stable renal hemodynamics over 12 weeks.

articles.title: Anti-Inflammatory effects of Vietnamese coriander (Persicaria odorata (Lour.) Soják) extract in a rat paw edema model and modulation of pro-inflammatory mediators.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persicaria odorata (Lour.) Soják, or Vietnamese coriander, is an edible plant traditionally used to address flatulence and localized inflammation. However, scientific evidence supporting its anti-inflammatory effects and molecular mechanisms remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the anti-inflammatory effects of 50% ethanolic leaf extract of P. odorata (PO) in a carrageenan-induced rat paw edema model and to elucidate its possible mechanisms of action. METHODS: PO was phytochemically characterized by identifying selected phytochemical markers using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Acute oral toxicity was evaluated in rats following the OECD Guideline 423. The anti-inflammatory activity was investigated using the carrageenan-induced paw edema model by assessing paw volume, histopathological changes, polymorphonuclear cell (PMN) infiltration, myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and inflammation-related gene expression. In silico studies were also conducted to investigate possible interactions between selected phytochemicals and inflammation-related targets. RESULTS: HPLC analysis confirmed the presence of gallic acid, rutin, myricetin, and quercetin as selected phytochemical markers. No evident acute toxicity was observed at the tested doses. In the carrageenan-induced paw edema model, PO significantly reduced paw volume, PMN infiltration, MPO activity, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels. Furthermore, PO significantly downregulated the mRNA expression of inflammation-related genes. In silico analyses suggested nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)- and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)-related pathways as potential molecular targets. CONCLUSIONS: PO possesses significant anti-inflammatory activity by suppressing inflammatory mediators and reducing inflammatory cell infiltration and may modulate NF-κB and MAPK-related pathways, as suggested by computational analyses.

articles.title: Visualization of acetamide-induced large micronucleus formation via nuclear atrophy in rat primary hepatocyte.
articles.abstract: Micronuclei are small nuclei that form when chromosomes or fragments fail to segregate into daughter nuclei during cell division. We previously suggested that acetamide induces the formation of large micronuclei through nuclear atrophy in binuclear hepatocytes. In this study, to confirm large micronuclei formation from atrophic nuclei within identical hepatocytes, we established an in vitro model. Large micronuclei formed from rat primary hepatocytes treated with 30 mM acetamide showing molecular features identical to those observed in vivo, including loss of nuclear lamina, accumulation of phosphorylated histone H2AX, and heterochromatinization. Time-lapse imaging demonstrated that large micronuclei were specifically formed due to unilateral nuclear atrophy in binuclear hepatocytes. Although nuclear atrophy was also observed in mononuclear hepatocytes, most hepatocytes with atrophic nuclei underwent subsequent cell death, whereas only a portion of binuclear hepatocytes generated large micronuclei and survived. These findings indicate that nuclear atrophy occurs in both mononuclear and binuclear hepatocytes and generally leads to cell death, whereas a subset of binuclear hepatocytes survives through large micronucleus formation. Atrophic nuclei exhibited a partial loss of nuclear lamina accompanied by DNA damage accumulation and chromatin condensation, whereas heterochromatinization was observed only in some of them, suggesting the involvement of nuclear rupture in large micronucleus formation. Overall, these data demonstrate a novel mechanism of large micronuclei formation through unilateral nuclear atrophy in binuclear hepatocytes independent of cell division. We propose the term "atrophic micronucleus" for this large micronucleus, which may mediate chromosomal rearrangements that contribute to acetamide hepatocarcinogenesis.

articles.title: Methiodone (IC-26) a case series: an old, but novel, opioid substance causing severe toxicity.
articles.abstract: Methiodone (IC-26; 4-ethylsulfonyl-N,N-dimethyl-4,4-diphenylbutan-2-amine) is a synthetic opioid derivative of methadone that has recently emerged on the designer drug market. Data on its clinical toxicity and pharmacokinetics remain limited. We describe four cases of severe methiodone intoxication requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, taking place between July and November 2025. Clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes were evaluated. In addition, systematic toxicological analysis was performed including Liquid Chromatography - High Resolution Mass Spectrometry (LC-HRMS) and targeted Liquid Chromatography - tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). All patients presented with a classical opioid toxidrome, characterized by respiratory depression, miosis, and decreased consciousness. Naloxone administration resulted in clinical improvement in all cases. Methiodone plasma concentrations ranged from 0.20 to 0.64 mg/L. The elimination half-life in plasma was estimated at approximately 13 h based on one case. Metabolite analysis revealed N-dealkylation as an important metabolic pathway, with additional hydroxylation and limited glucuronidation. Methiodone was variably detected in routine immunoassays, depending on assay specificity. No electrocardiogram (ECG) clinically relevant abnormalities were observed, in contrast to observations in methadone intoxications. Methiodone is an emerging opioid capable of causing severe, but treatable, intoxication. Increased clinical and analytical awareness is essential, as further cases are likely to emerge with the ongoing evolution of the new psychoactive substance market.

articles.title: Testing strategy for the identification of thyroid hormone system disrupting chemicals.
articles.abstract: Disruption of the thyroid hormone (TH) system during fetal and neonatal life poses a significant risk to human neurodevelopment, yet current regulatory assessments lack sufficiently sensitive and specific endpoints to identify chemicals causing TH system disruption (THSD). The ATHENA project aimed to develop an integrated framework combining in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches to improve the identification of substances causing THSD and support their assessment within a regulatory context. This testing strategy emphasizes increased use of the adverse outcome pathways (AOP) framework and read-across approaches to better predict and address adversity. It further provides recommendations for in silico and in vitro test batteries and targeted in vivo investigations to improve identification of chemicals causing THSD. In addition, we propose enhancements to current regulatory practice, including further standardization of test methods, improved integration of human epidemiological and cross-species evidence, and recognition of altered TH concentration in serum and brain in animal studies as predictors of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in humans. Collectively, these measures are intended to strengthen chemical hazard assessment and improve protection of human and environmental health through more robust and efficient identification of THSD.

articles.title: Systematic assessment of transcriptomic and phenotypic biological profiling for mechanism-based hazard assessment using target-annotated reference chemicals in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells.
articles.abstract: Integrating high-throughput in vitro data into next-generation risk assessment (NGRA) workflows requires screening strategies that yield quantitative potency estimates and mechanistically interpretable biological signals. Transcriptomic and morphological profiling are increasingly adopted for early-stage hazard identification by enabling triage of substances for resource-intensive follow-up and prioritizing candidates most likely to present meaningful risk. In this study, we aimed to characterize biological concordance and uncertainty by quantifying how well high-throughput transcriptomics (HTTr) and Cell Painting PLUS (CPP) bioactivity profiles recover target-relevant biological signals in immortalized human renal proximal tubule epithelial RPTEC/TERT1 cells using 313 reference chemicals with high-confidence target annotations. Through quality control procedures and biological activity filters we yielded 142 reference chemicals spanning 66 different targets, which were systematically evaluated for biological concentration-responses by HTTr and CPP. HTTr was evaluated using TXG-MAPr-based qualitative and quantitative gene network activity analysis. HTTr showed the most prominent activity for targets that were highest expressed in RPTEC/TERT1 cells. Active chemical-pairs showed strong gene network activity correlation albeit with different potencies. Similarly, the highest transcriptomic concordance was observed for reference chemicals acting in the same pathway, such as EGFR/MEK or PI3K/AKT/mTOR. CPP often showed high sensitivity primarily at the organelle level providing limited mechanistic insight for chemical grouping. Collectively, the results support HTTr and CPP as complementary early-tier assays within an in vitro weight-of-evidence safety testing framework. Although CPP is suitable as a cost-effective screening modality, HTTr offers higher mechanistic resolution for mode-of-action inference in high-throughput bioactivity screening and therefore remains necessary for high-confidence mechanistic interpretation.

articles.title: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling as a translational tool in forensic toxicology: from pig to human synthetic cannabinoid toxicokinetics using 5F-Cumyl-P7AICA and its major metabolite as a case study.
articles.abstract: Synthetic cannabinoids are increasingly associated with severe adverse events and fatalities. The SC 5F-Cumyl-P7AICA (5FC) is particularly concerning due to its high potency. Human studies of such compounds are ethically and practically constrained, highlighting the value of physiologically based pharmacokinetic/toxicokinetic (PBTK) modeling as a translational tool. Here, we developed a PBTK model for 5FC and its primary metabolite N-pentanoic acid (NPA) in pigs and translated it to humans for predicting systemic and tissue-specific exposure. Using the published toxicokinetic data in pigs receiving 200 µg/kg 5FC via intravenous (IV) and inhalation routes, a parent-metabolite PBTK model was built. Serum, whole blood, and fat tissue concentrations were used for calibration and evaluation. The model was used to predict various tissue concentrations in pigs as well as translated to humans using species-specific physiological parameters and in vitro-measured human plasma protein binding and subsequently compared with allometric scaling of a population TK model. The pig model accurately predicted mean concentration-time profiles (MRD: 1.49 and 2.19 for 5FC, 1.51 and 1.62 for NPA, IV and inhalation, respectively). Individual predictions fell within two-fold of observed values for all TK parameters. The human PBTK model predicted lower 5FC exposure compared to allometric scaling after both IV and inhalation dosing, while NPA exposure was comparable after IV and higher after inhalation dosing. Tissue-level simulations in humans showed organ-specific distribution patterns for both compounds. In conclusion, the PBTK model described 5FC and NPA disposition in pigs, including tissue concentrations and generated exploratory human systemic and tissue exposure predictions.

articles.title: Human in vitro hepatic models for steatosis: a harmonized comparison for studying drug metabolism.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic, inflammatory, and fibrotic processes which are not fully reproducible in vitro. However, MASLD is increasingly investigated using human-relevant in vitro models. This study models the steatosis component using a harmonized free fatty acid (FFA; oleic/palmitic acid) exposure across four human hepatic platforms: 2D primary human hepatocyte (PHH) suspension cultures, 2.5D PHH sandwich cultures, 3D PHH spheroids, and HepaRG/LX-2/HUVEC micro-organoids. Steatosis and function were assessed via lipid imaging, albumin/LDH release, mRNA profiling of drug metabolizing enzymes (DMEs) and transporters using Multiplex technology, and LC-MS/MS-based CYP1A2/CYP2C9 activity. Untreated cultures served as controls; FFA-treated cultures were designated "FFA-induced steatotic", reflecting lipid accumulation rather than full MASLD. PHH suspensions, classified a priori as putatively healthy or MASH based on medical records of the donor, showed rapid functional decline and substantial donor variability. In contrast, 2.5D sandwiches, 3D spheroids, and micro-organoids remained stable for 10-21 days and developed robust FFA-induced steatotic. Spheroids and micro-organoids maintained CYP activity and exhibited distinct metabolic responses; micro-organoids partially recovered after FFA-stimulus withdrawal. Cross-platform differences arise from both biological responses and model-intrinsic characteristics. 3D spheroids and micro-organoids were most suitable for long-term metabolic remodeling studies, while 2.5D sandwich cultures provided a practical system for transporter and enzyme induction research. Despite functional instability, 2D suspensions retained value for rapid short-term screening. These findings support use-case-driven selection of hepatic in vitro models for toxicology and ADME applications under FFA-induced steatosis.

articles.title: Comparative in vitro metabolic profiling of six novel methylthiophene cathinones using different human liver systems and LC-HRMS/MS.
articles.abstract: Synthetic cathinones represent a major class of new psychoactive substances associated with severe toxicological risks. Therapeutic cathinone derivatives such as amfepramone (appetite suppressant) were partially removed from the market due to severe side effects. p-Tolyl-substituted synthetic cathinones are primarily known as new psychoactive substances and are associated with serious adverse events and abuse liability. Bioisosteric replacement of the p-tolyl ring with a 5'-methylthiophene moiety has recently emerged as a structural optimization strategy in this class and has led to the evaluation of methylthiophenes, a novel class of cathinone analogues. Knowledge of their hepatic biotransformation is essential for reliable toxicological detection and risk assessment. This study investigated the in vitro hepatic metabolism of six novel methylthiophene cathinones, 5Me-NM-BT (5-methyl-N-methyl-butanothiophenone), 5Me-NM-VT (5-methyl-N-methyl-valerothiophenone), 5Me-NE-BT (5-methyl-N-ethyl-butanothiophenone), 5Me-NE-VT (5-methyl-N-ethyl-valerothiophenone), 5Me-αP-BT (5-methyl-α-pyrrolidino-butanothiophenone), and 5Me-αP-VT (5-methyl-α-pyrrolidino-valerothiophenone) using pooled human liver microsomes (pHLM), pooled human liver S9 fraction (pHLS9), and HepG2 cells. Metabolites were characterized using reversed-phase and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry. Additionally, recombinant human monooxygenases were screened to identify isoenzymes mediating initial phase I steps. In total, 48 phase I and two phase II metabolites could be tentatively identified. Within each subgroup, the compounds showed similar metabolic profiles. Isozyme mapping revealed consistent contributions of various enzymes, including CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 suggesting a low risk of metabolism-based drug-drug interactions or single-enzyme polymorphism impact. Hydroxylated metabolites at the 5'-methyl group were consistently abundant across all models and, in combination with the respective parent compounds, represent promising analytical targets for toxicological screening.

articles.title: Combined exposure to triphenyl phosphate and haloperidol alters hepatic lipid homeostasis and xenobiotic metabolism beyond single-compound effects.
articles.abstract: Disruption of hepatic lipid metabolism by chemicals can lead to steatosis or phospholipidosis. Toxicological risk assessment mainly focuses on individual compounds rather than on mixtures, which does not well reflect real-life exposure scenarios. Mixture effects of compounds that do not share similar modes of action are increasingly drawing attention, with several studies having shown toxicodynamic and toxicokinetic interactions leading to unexpected mixture effects. The aim of this study was to investigate how the mixture of a phospholipidosis inducer and a steatosis inducer affect hepatic lipid and xenobiotic metabolism in comparison to single-compound treatment. Hence, differentiated HepaRG cells were treated with haloperidol (1-100 µM HLP, phospholipidosis inducer) and triphenyl phosphate (1-100 µM TPP, steatosis inducer), alone and in combination (with 25 µM TPP or 20 µM HLP). Steatosis induction by TPP was diminished when TPP was present in a mixture with HLP, with the antagonistic effects likely being caused by interactions at the transcriptional level. Furthermore, toxicokinetic investigations revealed decreased cytochrome P450 (CYP) expression and activity, leading to synergistic effects of the mixture on cell viability and also a slight increase in phospholipidosis induction by HLP. In conclusion, the investigated mixture of HLP and TPP demonstrated non-additive effects on hepatic lipid and xenobiotic metabolism with complex toxicodynamic and toxicokinetic interplay. These findings highlight the challenges of predicting mixture interactions for risk assessment.

articles.title: Systematic review of atropine cost-effectiveness in childhood myopia management.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood myopia is a global public health concern, with rising prevalence and a significant economic burden due to complications like retinal detachment and macular degeneration. Low-dose atropine (LDA) range 0.01%-0.05% is a clinically effective intervention for slowing myopia progression. However, its economic value remains under-evaluated across diverse settings. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251009680) to assess the cost-effectiveness of atropine for myopia management in children. Four model-based economic evaluations met the inclusion criteria, from Hong Kong, New Zealand, Australia/China and France/United Kingdom. Two studies used Markov cohort state-transition models while two employed a cohort decision-analytic model with probabilistic simulation of refractive outcomes. All four economic evaluations adopted a societal perspective; each applied a 3% annual discount rate to costs in their analyses and reported sensitivity analyses around discounting. Time horizons ranged from 5 years for incident myopia to lifetime horizons capturing myopia complications and vision impairment. Across economic models, LDA was consistently found to be cost-effective or cost-saving compared with standard care. Reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) included approximately NZ$1,590 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained in a New Zealand Markov cost-utility model, and USD 220-275 per diopter spherical equivalent reduction in a 5-year Hong Kong cost-effectiveness analysis. Evidence from high- and middle-income settings indicates that low-dose atropine is a cost-effective strategy, particularly when long-term progression to high myopia and its associated complications is considered. In European settings, low-dose atropine demonstrated a favorable cost profile compared with standard correction in children at higher risk of myopia progression, with consistent findings of cost-neutrality or cost savings when downstream costs of high myopia were included. CONCLUSION: Studies demonstrate favourable economic value using diverse metrics, including cost per diopter reduction, cost ratios, and cost-utility estimates, rather than uniformly reported ICERs. Greater economic benefits are observed over longer time horizons, largely driven by the avoidance of high myopia-related complications and associated costs. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251009680, identifier PROSPERO CRD420251009680.

articles.title: Venlafaxine in oncology: supportive-care evidence and emerging preclinical anticancer signals: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Venlafaxine, a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, has been investigated in oncology for several supportive care indications and, more recently, for potential anticancer activity. However, the available evidence remains fragmented across clinical and preclinical studies. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence regarding the role of venlafaxine in oncology, including established supportive care applications and emerging anticancer potential. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to 22 August 2026. Original clinical and preclinical studies evaluating venlafaxine in cancer populations or experimental cancer models were eligible. Clinical and preclinical evidence was synthesized separately using a narrative approach. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools for clinical studies and the SYRCLE Risk of Bias tool for animal studies. RESULTS: 25 studies were included, comprising 23 clinical studies and 2 preclinical studies. The strongest clinical evidence supported venlafaxine for treatment-related hot flashes, particularly among breast cancer survivors receiving endocrine therapy, with the strongest randomized, placebo-controlled trial evidence showing significantly greater reductions with venlafaxine than placebo (P < 0.0001 for higher doses); within-group percentage reductions are also reported but should not be interpreted as treatment effects. Evidence for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy was inconsistent, with potential benefit for acute oxaliplatin-related neurotoxicity but insufficient support for prevention or routine treatment of chronic CIPN. Evidence for other supportive care outcomes, including oral mucositis-associated pain, fatigue, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and quality of life, was limited. Venlafaxine was generally well tolerated, although adverse effects varied by dose and comparator. Preclinical studies investigated anticancer activity, but not equivalently: one in melanoma models showed direct antiproliferative/pro-apoptotic effects of venlafaxine via JNK1/2-Nur77 signaling, whereas a colorectal cancer study showed only context-dependent antagonism of norepinephrine-driven tumor progression, with no significant effect of venlafaxine alone. No clinical evidence currently supports venlafaxine as a direct anticancer treatment. CONCLUSION: Venlafaxine has an established evidence-based role in supportive oncology for treatment-related hot flashes, whereas its role in CIPN and other supportive care indications remains uncertain. Emerging anticancer findings are limited to preclinical models and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Further randomized clinical trials are needed for supportive care indications, while additional mechanistic and preclinical validation is required before venlafaxine can be considered for clinical evaluation as an anticancer therapy.

articles.title: Reduction through refinement: bridging animal studies and NAMs through 'omics technologies enriched regulatory studies.
Circulating biomarkers linking heart failure and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: Toward an integrated biological framework - A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexist and are associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization. Accumulating evidence suggests that these conditions also share biological mechanisms that contribute to disease progression. However, although numerous circulating biomarkers have been investigated in both conditions, their interpretation has largely remained disease-specific, limiting a broader understanding of the biological processes underlying HF-COPD coexistence. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA 2020 recommendations to identify and critically evaluate circulating biomarkers shared by HF and COPD according to their diagnostic, prognostic, and pathophysiological significance. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by Google Scholar and backward citation searching, identified 23 eligible studies published between 2015 and 2026. Natriuretic peptides, particularly N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, were the most extensively investigated biomarkers for identifying cardiac dysfunction and predicting adverse outcomes. Cardiac troponins, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis- and remodelling-related biomarkers, endothelial markers, and metabolic biomarkers provided complementary insights into distinct biological pathways involved in disease progression. Overall, the available evidence indicates that circulating biomarkers reflect complementary pathophysiological processes, providing a rationale for future evaluation of multimarker approaches. By integrating these findings within a common biological context, this review highlights the potential of multimarker approaches for future investigation in cardiopulmonary risk stratification and translational research.

articles.title: Glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD)-65 antibodies-associated autoimmune neurological syndrome.
articles.abstract: Glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 antibody-associated neurological syndrome (GAD65-AINS) is an autoimmune disorder mediated by anti-GAD65 antibodies, with clinical phenotypes including stiff-person spectrum disorders(SPS), limbic encephalitis, cerebellar ataxia, and drug-resistant epilepsy. As the rate-limiting enzyme in GABA synthesis, GAD65 exhibits conformational plasticity, which forms the molecular basis for autoimmune targeting. Genetic susceptibility involves HLA regions (DR3, DR4) and non-HLA immune regulatory genes (e.g., PTPN22, CTLA4), demonstrating a polygenic characteristic. Pathogenic mechanisms involve T-cell-mediated cellular immunity, direct functional interference by antibodies, complement-dependent humoral immune effects, and synergistic enhancement of pathological effects by coexisting antibodies (e.g., anti-CN1A). Diagnosis requires integration of clinical phenotypes, quantitative antibody testing (serum ELISA ≥10,000 IU/mL or RIA ≥20 nmol/L), intrathecal synthesis evidence in CSF, and imaging evaluation. High-titer antibodies are the core diagnostic basis for SPS, but must be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings.Treatment follows a stratified principle: symptomatic management is based on GABAergic enhancers, while immunotherapy includes IVIg, glucocorticoids, and rituximab, etc. Treatment responses vary significantly across phenotypes, with better responses observed in SPS and limbic encephalitis, followed by cerebellar ataxia, and limited responses in GAD65-related epilepsy, often requiring adjunctive antiepileptic drugs. Most patients require long-term immunomodulatory therapy. Future research should elucidate the synergistic mechanisms between T cells and antibodies, develop biomarkers, explore novel targeted therapies such as FcRn antagonists, and promote the transformation of precision medicine models.

articles.title: Microenvironment-guided design of non-viral gene delivery systems: from biological cues to therapeutic translation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Non-viral gene delivery systems offer adaptable alternatives to viral vectors for gene therapy. Nevertheless, their clinical translation remains limited by biological barriers and the pathological tissue microenvironment. Tumors exhibit alterations in the tissue microenvironment, including extracellular acidosis, altered redox balance, elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS), dysregulated enzymatic activity, and hypoxia, which can serve as endogenous cues for designing stimulus-responsive gene delivery systems with site-specific cargo release. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines tumor microenvironment-responsive non-viral gene delivery systems and discusses how disease-specific biological cues can be integrated into carrier design. We distinguish disease-associated tissue cues from intracellular triggers such as endosomal acidification and evaluate how these stimuli influence carrier stability, cellular interactions, intracellular trafficking, and therapeutic efficacy, while considering trade-offs in sensitivity, specificity, safety, and manufacturability. Relevant literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for English-language studies published between 2010 and 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Emphasizing the transition from material-driven approaches toward biology-guided design, this review proposes an integrated decision framework to guide the design and translational evaluation of microenvironment-responsive non-viral gene delivery systems. It highlights translation challenges, including microenvironmental heterogeneity, manufacturing and scalability challenges, and safety and regulatory considerations.

articles.title: Ginsenosides in hematopoietic homeostasis and hematological malignancies: context-dependent pharmacological effects and translational limitations.
articles.abstract: Ginseng has long been used as a botanical drug in East Asian traditional medical systems, particularly in China and Korea, and as a food ingredient. Ginsenosides are specialized metabolites of Panax species with diverse pharmacological activities reported in experimental studies. Evidence regarding their effects in hematological contexts, however, is dispersed across studies using different materials, models, and exposure conditions. This Mini Review synthesizes findings from purified ginsenosides and chemically characterized saponin fractions, focusing on hematopoietic and immune regulation in non-malignant stress models and on malignant hematopoietic cell fate. In non-malignant models, selected metabolites and fractions were associated with reduced cellular injury and changes in peripheral blood, phenotypic, or colony-forming endpoints. In malignant models, effects on proliferation, apoptosis, differentiation, autophagy, and drug transport were reported mainly in cell lines. Clinical evidence remains limited, while gaps in material standardization and pharmacologically relevant exposure constrain translation. By comparing non-malignant and malignant contexts, this review provides an integrated framework for interpreting heterogeneous findings and highlights how metabolite identity, experimental model, cellular context, and exposure may influence the reported effects.

articles.title: Overcoming adaptive resistance in non-small cell lung cancer: integrating targeted therapies, immunotherapy synergy, and nanocarrier delivery.
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death, characterized by high mortality rates, tumor adaptation and heterogeneity, and immune evasion mechanisms. Despite recent advancements in chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery, survival rates for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remain low, signifying the need for new strategies and innovative treatments. This review explores the combinatorial potential of immunotherapy with direct targeting of tumor growth to address the multifaceted challenges of NSCLC. Key approaches include small-molecule inhibitors, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibition, angiogenesis inhibition, and nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems. Nanocarrier systems enable coordinated drug release and pharmacological synergy, thereby ensuring effective inhibition of pathways in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Additionally, this review addresses several resistance mechanisms in the context of specific inhibitors (e.g., EGFR and ALK inhibitors). Translational insights help bridge preclinical findings to clinical applications with an emphasis on angiogenesis inhibition and personalized approaches. Ethical considerations such as consent and preclinical safety testing are emphasized to ensure the safe development of these therapies. With the new generation of genetic engineering, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies for tumor growth, this work discusses the potential to transform lung cancer treatment.

articles.title: Pharmacoepigenetics: from epigenetic regulation to personalized therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Pharmacoepigenetics is an emerging field of precision medicine that examines how epigenetic modifications influence interindividual variability in drug response. This review discusses the clinical utility of epigenetic therapy in personalized medicine. Current FDA-approved epigenetic drugs including DNA methyltransferase inhibitors, histone deacetylase inhibitors, EZH2 inhibitors, mutant IDH inhibitors, and menin inhibitors are reviewed along with emerging therapies such as BET inhibitors, LSD1 inhibitors, precision epigenetic editing, and combination treatment strategies. Despite notable advances, challenges such as target selectivity, dose-limiting toxicity, epigenetic variability and lack of biomarkers for predicting response or selecting patients continue to limit broader clinical implementation of epigenetic drugs. Continued progress is expected to expand the role of pharmacoepigenetics and improve treatment across a growing range of diseases other than oncology.

articles.title: IL-11 in fibrostenotic Crohn's disease: historical agonism, the selective-inhibition hypothesis, and evidence thresholds for translation.
articles.abstract: Effective medical treatment for fibrostenotic Crohn's disease remains a major unmet clinical need. This narrative review examines whether high stromal interleukin-11 (IL-11) identifies a pharmacologically reversible dependency in established fibrostenotic disease or mainly marks advanced remodeling. Historical trials found schedule-dependent activity of recombinant human IL-11, but an active-comparator trial showed inferior remission induction compared with prednisolone. In mice, Il11 or Il11ra1 deficiency worsened epithelial apoptosis and acute dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) colitis. By contrast, inducible Il11 deletion during repeated DSS injury reduced collagen deposition and hydroxyproline with broadly similar inflammatory trajectories. These contrasting findings support context-dependent effects across acute injury and chronic remodeling. Human tissue, serum and treatment-response studies associate IL-11 with fibrostenosis and stromal activation, but do not establish that an IL-11-high lesion responds to selective inhibition. Differences in fibroblast state, tissue compartment and treatment timing could therefore influence both efficacy and harm. Early LASN01 studies outside inflammatory bowel disease support systemic target engagement and preliminary tolerability; intestinal efficacy remains untested. The decisive next test is selective inhibition after a structural lesion is documented, with verified intestinal exposure and separate structural, inflammatory and repair outcomes. This would distinguish reduced collagen accumulation during disease development from reversal of an established Crohn's stricture.

articles.title: Research on the molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of reactive oxygen species in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) exhibits significant geographical clustering and etiological heterogeneity. It is particularly prevalent in Southeast Asia and is typically associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection.
