Reactive oxygen species (ROS), as highly reactive oxygen metabolites, play a key role in regulating cellular signaling and maintaining redox homeostasis. Although the role of ROS in tumors has been well established, reviews examining how ROS influence NPC and their potential therapeutic applications remain relatively scarce. ROS exert diverse effects in NPC, including roles in EBV-associated processes, regulation of programmed cell death, metabolic reprogramming, formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and epigenetic remodeling. In addition, natural small-molecule compounds that regulate ROS levels and emerging combination therapy strategies have considerable therapeutic potential in NPC. This review discusses the dual role of ROS in NPC, examines their contributions to disease development, and further explores how these mechanisms could inform the design of ROS-targeted therapies, as well as the associated translational challenges.

articles.title: Clitoria ternatea as a phytopharmacological resource: plant metabolites, mechanistic evidence, translational prospects, and safety considerations.
articles.abstract: Clitoria ternatea L. (Fabaceae; butterfly pea) is used in traditional medicine and is increasingly developed as a food colorant, functional beverage, botanical preparation, and source of peptide scaffolds. Previous reviews have separately emphasized ethnomedicine, flower extraction, anthocyanins, or cyclotides; however, the evidence has rarely been integrated according to preparation identity, study design, bioavailability, safety, and translational readiness. This structured critical narrative review updates the literature through 8 August 2026. PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar were searched using species-name and domain-specific terms. Primary studies were prioritized, and evidence was stratified as chemical/analytical, in silico, isolated-target or cell-based, animal, and human. Study interpretation considered taxonomic authentication, plant part, extraction and chemical characterization, dose, controls, duration, model relevance, adverse-event reporting, and exposure plausibility. The principal metabolite classes are ternatin anthocyanins, flavonol glycosides, phenolic acids, triterpenoids, sterols, and cyclotides. Chemical assays such as DPPH and ABTS support redox characterization but do not establish pharmacological or therapeutic efficacy. Neurobehavioral, anti-inflammatory, metabolic, antimicrobial, organ-protective, and cytotoxic signals are reported mainly in preclinical models, often using incompletely standardized extracts. Human evidence is restricted to small acute crossover studies and exploratory adjunctive studies, including a 2026 study of flower tea in people with type 2 diabetes and diabetic distress. Intact ternatins are orally absorbed in rats, but systemic exposure is modest and human pharmacokinetic data are unavailable; metabolite exposure, formulation effects, chronic toxicity, reproductive safety, cyclotide immunogenicity, and botanical-drug interactions remain insufficiently defined. Recent genomic and peptide studies strengthen the biotechnology relevance of cyclotides and butelase-1 but should not be conflated with the efficacy of crude botanical preparations. Overall, C. ternatea is a promising source of defined food, botanical, and peptide products, but therapeutic claims require authenticated materials, marker-based standardization, exposure-linked pharmacology, and adequately controlled clinical trials.

articles.title: The synergistic potential of combining PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapies in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is associated with a poor prognosis, and the efficacy of conventional therapies (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery) remains limited. The advent of programmed death 1 (PD-1)/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitors has substantially altered the treatment paradigm for ESCC. The combination of these immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with conventional treatments demonstrates significant synergistic potential. Standard oncological regimens often center on chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, or various combinations thereof. This synergy stems from complementary mechanisms: conventional therapies can induce immunogenic cell death, release tumor antigens, and remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, thereby laying the groundwork for immunotherapy. In turn, PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors work by releasing the "brakes" on T cells, activating and enhancing the host anti-tumor immune response. This facilitates the elimination of residual cancer cells and establishes long-term immune surveillance. In conclusion, the combination of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapy achieves a greater-than-additive ("1 + 1>2") effect and has evolved into a standard first-line treatment strategy for advanced/metastatic ESCC, substantially improving patient outcomes. Future research will focus on optimizing combination protocols, overcoming resistance, and precisely identifying patient populations most likely to benefit.

articles.title: The Patient Perspectives of Clinical Pharmacist Services in Hospitals and Clinics: A Focused Narrative Review of Qualitative Studies.
articles.abstract: Patient perspectives are highly important to ensure optimal patient care in hospitals or primary care settings. Clinical pharmacy services, in which clinical pharmacists provide direct patient care, are a relatively recent addition to healthcare and are increasing in scope and availability. In this focused narrative review, relevant qualitative studies describing patients' perspectives after the integration of clinical pharmacists into healthcare services were included. Patients described predominantly positive feedback, presented as facilitators. The facilitators described in studies were that patients felt safe, experienced clear communication and collaboration with pharmacists, increased their knowledge of medications, and appreciated pharmacists' time and availability. Occasionally, patients described challenges with the pharmacist or service, presented as barriers. The barriers were that patients were unfamiliar with the clinical pharmacists' role and services, lacked trust or experienced conflicting information, experienced a lack of patient-centredness, and some disagreed or had challenges with elements of the intervention. In conclusion, most perspectives represented positive facilitators that should be kept and protected in the future, with some barriers that can be overcome in the future for optimal patient care and development of clinical pharmacy services.

articles.title: Developing physiologically based pharmacokinetic models to understand lactation exposure to medications: Gaps in available data and call for action.
articles.abstract: Although a significant proportion of postpartum women use medication whilst breastfeeding, information regarding infant exposure to maternal medication via the breast milk is typically limited. In addition to growing pressures for the generation of clinical lactation data from regulators, interest in the use of alternative techniques, such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling, to support clinical studies in this underserved population is increasing. This is consistent with the current interest in model-informed drug development. For lactation models to contribute to clinical decision making, the uncertainties underpinning these models must be understood and minimized where possible. This review therefore aimed to investigate the breast milk distribution models used to support PBPK modelling in the lactation context and to characterize the sources and extent of uncertainty associated with these models. Three models were identified throughout the literature, termed as the Phase Distribution, Log-Transformed Phase Distribution, and Semi-Mechanistic models. Model performance, as compared against observed data, was broadly consistent between each of the three models but significant limitations were identified. Specifically, there is a paucity of clinical lactation data in which breast milk constituents are adequately defined to allow validation of mechanistic models; in vitro data inconsistently support model assumptions; and limited data have been generated using samples from a range of women to offer an understanding of population variability. These gaps in available data are clearly addressable, and further work should be conducted to better support the use of modelling and help address the inequities in safe access to medicine currently faced by women who breastfeed their infants.

articles.title: Mucoadhesive microspheres of parthenolide nanocrystals for sustained drug delivery and its potential cytotoxic effect against hepatic cancers.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The current focus in drug delivery system design is Mucoadhesion. Mucoadhesive microspheres are designed to remain at the drug delivery site for a longer period by enhancing contact with the absorption surface, thereby improving the drug's systemic exposure. The study aimed to formulate and assess mucoadhesive microspheres using sodium alginate, guar gum, and carbopol to achieve sustained release of parthenolide nanocrystals, thereby increasing systemic exposure. METHODS: The ionic gelation process was employed to prepare parthenolide-loaded microspheres (PTL-NC-M). The microspheres were characterized for their particle size (P.S.), entrapment efficiency (E.E.), mucoadhesivity, swelling capacity, and drug release profile, as well as by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and an in vitro wash-off test. RESULTS: The selected formulation F2 has a particle size of 3.10 ± 0.18 µm and a percentage swelling index of 132.67 ± 1.67%. The carbopol content plays a crucial role in mucoadhesion, and the F2 exhibited superior adhesion to the membranes. The entrapment efficiency ranged from 43% to 95%. The SEM analysis revealed continuous polymeric-coated spherical microspheres. CONCLUSION: The microspheres demonstrated a prolonged residence time during the in vitro wash-off period, along with the desired drug release profile. The selected microspheres F2 exhibited better and sustained drug release, along with good mucoadhesivity, resulting in an enhanced invitro cytotoxic potential and increased systemic exposure.

articles.title: Liposomal Kasugamycin attenuates methylmercury chloride-induced neurotoxicity through modulation of CHI3L1-associated neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Methylmercury chloride (CH₃HgCl)-induced neurotoxicity is associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, glutamate dysregulation, apoptosis, and progressive neuronal injury. Chitinase-3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1) plays an important role in neuroinflammatory processes and represents a potential therapeutic target in neurodegenerative disorders. Kasugamycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic primarily used in agriculture as a bactericide and fungicide. Beyond its agricultural applications, kasugamycin exhibits anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties; however, its potential therapeutic application in neurological disorders is limited by poor brain penetration and limited pharmacokinetic characteristics. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective potential of liposomal kasugamycin against CH₃HgCl-induced neurotoxicity in rats. Kasugamycin-loaded liposomes were prepared using the thin-film hydration technique and optimized through a Central Composite Design approach. The optimized formulation was characterized for physicochemical properties and in vitro drug release before evaluation in a rat model of CH₃HgCl-induced neurotoxicity. Neuroprotective efficacy was assessed using behavioral, biochemical, molecular, and histopathological parameters. The optimized formulation exhibited nanoscale particle size and high encapsulation efficiency. Liposomal kasugamycin significantly improved locomotor performance and body weight while attenuating oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis-related alterations, glutamate dysregulation, and neuronal injury. Treatment restored superoxide dismutase (SOD) and reduced glutathione (GSH) levels while decreasing malondialdehyde (MDA), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), Bax, caspase-3, and glutamate levels. Furthermore, liposomal kasugamycin increased Bcl-2 and myelin basic protein (MBP) expression and modulated CHI3L1 expression, suggesting potential involvement of neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective pathways. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first evidence of the neuroprotective potential of liposomal kasugamycin against CH₃HgCl-induced neurotoxicity, supporting further investigation of this formulation as a potential therapeutic strategy for mercury-associated neuronal injury.

articles.title: Pharmacological activation of sigma-1 receptor by clinically approved drugs enhances KV1.5 channel activity in the pulmonary circulation.
articles.abstract: Sigma-1 receptor (S1R) is a ligand-operated chaperone involved in the modulation of ion channel function, including the voltage-gated potassium (KV) channels such as KV1.5. KV1.5 channel dysfunction is a characteristic feature of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), and its pharmacological modulation represents an attractive strategy in this context. Here, we investigated whether pharmacological activation of S1R by clinically approved drugs, such as dimemorfan and fluoxetine, enhances KV1.5 channel activity in pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). KV currents were recorded using whole-cell patch-clamp in freshly isolated PASMCs from rats, humans, and rats with experimental PAH induced by SU5416 plus hypoxia (SuHx). Pulmonary vascular reactivity was assessed was assessed in isolated pulmonary arteries using wire myography, and protein expression was analysed by Western blot. Dimemorfan and fluoxetine significantly increased DPO-1-sensitive KV currents, corresponding to the KV1.5 component, without affecting DPO-1-insensitive currents. These effects were abolished by pharmacological blockade of S1R, supporting a S1R-dependent mechanism. Increased KV1.5 activity was associated with reduced pulmonary vasoconstrictor responses. The KV1.5-enhancing effects of both compounds were also observed in PASMCs from PAH rats. The ability of dimemorfan to enhance KV currents was also confirmed in freshly isolated human PASMCs. Overall, these findings support a role of S1R as a pharmacological regulator of KV1.5 channel function and provide evidence that clinically approved S1R-active drugs can enhance KV1.5 activity in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle. This pharmacological approach may provide a basis for further investigation of drug repurposing strategies targeting KV1.5 channel dysfunction in PAH.

articles.title: Multi-Omics Profiling of Cigarette Smoke-Associated Changes in Cell Models of Human Liver, Intestine and Lung.
articles.abstract: Cigarette smoke is a complex mixture that affects toxicological and pharmacological mechanisms in multiple organs, including liver, intestine, and lung. Therefore, an integrated multi-omics approach was applied to characterize cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced effects across human in vitro models of liver, intestine and lung. Primary human hepatocytes, biopsy-derived intestinal organoids, alveolar A549 cells, primary bronchial and small airway epithelial cells were exposed to CSE and analyzed using RNA sequencing and untargeted proteomics. Across tissues and omics-layers, activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signaling and strong induction of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 was identified as cross-tissue response. CYP1A1 was the only overlapping molecule among deregulated proteins across all in vitro models. Consistent deregulation of G protein-coupled receptor-signaling was observed. Overall, tissue-specific adaptations were identified. Liver models showed upregulation of xenobiotic and metabolic pathways, intestine models displayed downregulation of cell cycle processes consistent with growth arrest. Lung models should be considered cautiously because of heterogeneity between cell models but demonstrated a shared response of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 deregulation. Cross-omics comparisons of RNA sequencing and proteomics data revealed moderate correlations (ρ = 0.43-0.64) and limited overlap of individual molecules, highlighting the importance of post-transcriptional regulation. Network and upstream regulator analyses predicted a coordinated stress response accompanied by modulation of inflammatory signaling. These findings demonstrate that cigarette smoke induces shared pathway-level responses, alongside tissue-specific adaptations. This underscores the importance of considering multiple organ systems in toxicological and pharmacological assessments. This comprehensive dataset provides a resource that may support further hypothesis-driven analysis of cigarette smoke-related mechanisms.

articles.title: Tributyl phosphate disrupts neuronal autophagy: potential involvement of TLR4 in cell and rat models.
articles.abstract: Tributyl phosphate (TBP), a widely used organophosphate ester, exhibits lipophilic characteristics that enable it to cross the blood-brain barrier. Although its neurotoxicity has been confirmed, the underlying molecular pathways remain unclear. This study examined whether TLR4-associated autophagy disruption contributes to TBP-induced neuronal damage. Autophagy was activated with rapamycin (RAPA) and TLR4 was knocked down using siRNA. TBP exposure upregulated TLR4 expression and downregulated autophagy-related markers. Autophagic flux analysis assays using bafilomycin A1 further revealed that TBP impaired autophagosome biogenesis instead of lysosomal dysfunction. Autophagy activation and TLR4 knockdown each partially attenuated TBP-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and alterations in neuroinjury markers. Moreover, inhibiting TLR4 partially reversed the decrease in autophagy levels caused by TBP. Molecular docking predicted TBP may bind to the TLR4 extracellular domain, providing a testable framework for future validation. These findings identify TLR4-regulated autophagy suppression as a candidate mechanism for TBP neurotoxicity.

articles.title: Dendrobium officinale extract ameliorates Alzheimer's disease by modulating PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and autophagy-related processes: An integrated study combining feature-based molecular networking, network pharmacology and multi-omics.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder with limited effective treatments. Dendrobium officinale Kimura & Migo (D. officinale) has been traditionally used for dementia, but its active constituents and mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically characterize the chemical constituents of D. officinale extract (DOE) and elucidate its anti-AD mechanisms using an integrated pharmacological strategy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical composition of DOE was analyzed using UHPLC-Q-TOF/MS combined with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN). Target prediction and pathway analysis were performed using a network pharmacology approach. Therapeutic effects were evaluated in 5×FAD mice using behavioral and histopathological assays. Mechanistic validation was further conducted using transcriptomics, proteomics, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and molecular docking. RESULTS: Sixty-five components were identified, with apigenin, naringenin, rutin and oxyresveratrol as major identified constituents. Integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology analyses highlighted the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and autophagy-related processes as potential mechanisms underlying the anti-AD effects of DOE. In 5×FAD mice, DOE markedly improved cognitive deficits, alleviated hippocampal neuronal injury, reduced Aβ plaque deposition, and suppressed astrocytic and microglial activation. Mechanistically, DOE significantly downregulated the mRNA expression of Pi3k, Akt, and Mtor, reduced AKT and mTOR phosphorylation, and showed a trend toward decreased PI3K phosphorylation. DOE also reduced p62 accumulation and increased the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, suggesting an improvement in autophagy-related processes. Molecular docking further demonstrated favorable binding affinities of major identified constituents toward key targets, particularly AKT1 and PIK3CA. CONCLUSION: DOE ameliorates AD-related pathological changes, potentially through modulation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and improvement of autophagy-related processes. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting the potential of D. officinale as a multi-target therapeutic candidate for AD.

articles.title: Yiqi Jiedu Formula Suppresses Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Growth in Association with Glycerophospholipid Metabolism Remodeling: An Integrated Metabolomics and Lipidomics Study.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yiqi Jiedu formula (YQJDF), a classical traditional Chinese medicine prescription, has been used in the clinical management of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Although its therapeutic potential has been indicated by clinical experience, the molecular mechanisms through which it reprograms the intratumoral lipid metabolism remain uncharacterized. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically elucidate the antitumor mechanisms of YQJDF by profiling lipid metabolic alterations in tumor tissues through an integrated approach combining non-targeted metabolomics and lipidomics, and identify and validate the key enzymatic regulators of lipid metabolism modulated by the formula. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Non-targeted metabolomics was first performed to map globally altered metabolic pathways in tumor tissues. Subsequently, lipidomics was conducted, with exploratory differential lipids identified using a nominal P value < 0.05 and an OPLS-DA VIP score > 1, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Differential lipids were subjected to hierarchical clustering and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. Molecular docking was employed to predict the binding affinity of major formula constituents to key enzymes in enriched pathways, and the expression of candidate targets was validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC). RESULTS: Non-targeted metabolomics revealed that YQJDF significantly influenced sphingolipid metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, and galactose metabolism. Lipidomics identified 597 exploratory differential lipids , with 179 upregulated and 418 downregulated, of which only PA(P-30:8_18:0), PG(20:4_22:5), and SM(t36:3) remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (FDR < 0.05 and VIP > 1). Clustering analysis showed that these differential lipids were concentrated in phospholipid subclasses. KEGG enrichment analysis pinpointed three core pathways: Choline metabolism in cancer, Efferocytosis, and Glycerophospholipid metabolism. The convergent enrichment of glycerophospholipid metabolism by both omics platforms established it as a prominent pathway associated with treatment. Accordingly, molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities between key formula constituents and critical glycerophospholipid enzymes, including PGS1 and PLA2G4A. IHC showed lower PGS1 and PTDSS1 expression and higher PISD and PLA2G4A expression in the YQ and 3YQ groups compared with the control group. CEPT1 expression was significantly reduced only in the 3YQ group, with a non-significant downward trend in the YQ group. CONCLUSIONS: YQJDF treatment showed antitumor effects and was accompanied by extensive lipid metabolic remodeling in NPC tissues. Glycerophospholipid metabolism may represent an important metabolic pathway associated with YQJDF treatment, and several lipid-metabolism-related enzymes were identified as molecular candidates for further mechanistic investigation. These findings provide a basis for further validation of the role of lipid metabolic alterations in the antitumor response to YQJDF.

articles.title: CRYAB as a key mediator of Xianlian Jiedu Decoction-induced suppression of colorectal cancer stemness.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xianlian Jiedu Decoction (XLJDD) has long been used clinically in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). Our preliminary work indicated that XLJDD exerts anti-CRC activity by attenuating inflammation, restoring gut microbiota balance, and modulating signaling pathways such as CXCR2/PI3K/AKT. However, the bioactive constituents and the precise molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly defined. The present study sought to clarify the active components and mechanisms of XLJDD in CRC, thereby providing a scientific basis for its further therapeutic application. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effect of XLJDD on tumor stemness in CRC and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An orthotopic CRC mouse model was established and treated with XLJDD for 21 days. The chemical constituents of XLJDD were characterized by UPLC-MS/MS, and treatment-related metabolic alterations were profiled by plasma metabolomics. Tumor tissues were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing to identify differentially expressed genes, which were validated by Western blot and immunohistochemistry. In vitro, HCT116 and HT29 cells were evaluated for proliferation, sphere-forming capacity, stemness-marker (CD44/CD133) populations by flow cytometry, and protein expression by Western blot. CRYAB-knockdown cell lines were generated to assess proliferation (CCK-8), apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, and stemness-marker expression. Transcriptome sequencing combined with Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) was performed across treatment groups (NC, NC+XLJDD, CRYAB-KD, CRYAB-KD+XLJDD) to define the downstream signaling pathways regulated by XLJDD. RESULTS: XLJDD significantly suppressed tumor growth in the orthotopic CRC model. Plasma metabolomics revealed clear separation between groups, with reduced phenylalanine and glycerophospholipid metabolism and enhanced energy metabolism in XLJDD-treated mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumors identified cancer-cell clusters with high CRYAB and ALDH3A1 expression that were markedly suppressed following XLJDD treatment. In vitro, XLJDD reduced proliferation, sphere formation, CD44+/CD133+ populations, and stemness-marker expression. CRYAB knockdown impaired proliferation, induced apoptosis and G1-phase arrest, and attenuated stem-like features in CRC cells. Transcriptomic profiling with IPA identified STC1 as a downstream target of CRYAB, with the CRYAB-STC1 axis closely linked to the core stemness transcription factors OCT4, SOX2, and NANOG. DISCUSSION: These findings indicate that XLJDD constrains CRC stemness through a CRYAB-driven regulatory program rather than a single isolated target. By coupling CRYAB to STC1 and the OCT4/SOX2/NANOG network, the study connects XLJDD's anti-tumor activity to a defined stemness axis and positions CRYAB as a tractable node within it. Because CRYAB knockdown both reproduced and reinforced the anti-stemness effect of XLJDD, the data suggest that XLJDD acts, at least in part, by downregulating CRYAB, offering a mechanistic rationale that extends beyond its previously reported anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates for the first time that XLJDD suppresses CRC tumor stemness by targeting the CRYAB-STC1 axis. By integrating metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation, this work provides new evidence that XLJDD regulates cancer stemness and offers experimental support for its therapeutic potential in CRC.

articles.title: Advancing biophysics: semi-automated monitoring of protein aggregation kinetics to complement development of biopharmaceutics.
articles.abstract: Protein aggregation is a key stability challenge in biopharmaceutical development, requiring accelerated, predictive assessments to support early formulation development. Current approaches rely on indirect biophysical stability indicators or Arrhenius based kinetic modelling of accelerated conditions, which remains time and resource intensive. Kinetic analysis of protein aggregation based on Simultaneous Multiple Sample Light Scattering (SMSLS) provides a rapid and direct alternative, by enabling aggregation rate measurements under defined isothermal conditions in minimal volume (∼ 100 µL) and optional stirring stress. This work provides a first readiness assessment of SMSLS for protein formulation development. Implementation of automated data evaluation, including baseline detection, polynomial fitting, and establishment of an operational reference point (relative Mw/Mo = 1.5), substantially reduced user-related variability and allowed systematic characterization of experimental variation. Stress dependent effects were identified as the main driver of variability, while the method demonstrated good run-to-run performance across multiple protein formats, supported by the establishment of a standard reference. Based on this method understanding, the applicability to protein formulation development was shown for three case studies on buffer, pH and excipient selection utilizing both thermal and stirring stress. These findings position SMSLS as a high-throughput, low-volume approach for direct aggregation assessment, complementing biophysical characterization and extending it towards mechanical stress. These capabilities open new opportunities for comprehensive developability evaluation and informed biologics development roadmaps.

articles.title: Folate-decorated nanoparticles deliver bulleyaconitine A to inflammatory macrophages for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by synovial inflammatory cell infiltration and progressive joint erosion. Macrophages undergo a pathological shift toward an M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype, which plays a critical role in the progression of the disease. Modulation of M1 macrophages may be a promising therapeutic strategy. Herein, we developed folic acid-functionalized PLGA nanoparticles (FA-PLGA NPs) for targeted delivery of an anti-inflammatory natural compound, bulleyaconitine A (BLA), into M1 macrophages. The nanoparticles exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 151.91 ± 5.41 nm with a polydispersity index of 0.153 ± 0.016, a negative zeta potential (-13.50 ± 0.82 mV), a high encapsulation efficiency of 90.0%, and excellent colloidal stability. In vitro, FA-PLGA NPs were efficiently internalized by M1-polarized RAW264.7 macrophages via folate receptor-mediated endocytosis, and the uptake level was 7.79-fold higher than non-targeted NPs. Exposure to the NPs significantly reduced the population of CD86-positive M1 cells and decreased iNOS expression while increasing Arg-1 expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of pro-inflammatory and tissue-destructive pathways and upregulation of myeloid differentiation and immune regulation genes. In an adjuvant-induced arthritis rat model, FA-PLGA NPs treatment resulted in significant alleviation of paw swelling, joint destruction, and cartilage proteoglycan loss, as well as a decrease in the levels of serum IL-6 and TNF-α. Encouragingly, the nanoparticle formulation exhibited favorable in vivo safety, with no observable adverse effects on major organs. Collectively, FA‑PLGA NPs effectively modulated M1 macrophages and achieved potent anti‑arthritic efficacy with improved safety, demonstrating their potential as a nanotherapeutic for RA management.

articles.title: Evaluating near-infrared spectroscopy and multivariate modelling for predicting dissolution profiles of 3D printed extended-release tablets.
articles.abstract: Non-destructive quality control strategies are essential to enable production of personalised printlets (3D printed tablets). The prediction of dissolution behaviour from printlet-specific data, such as spectroscopic, remains underexplored. In this study, we demonstrate the use of multimodal data consisting of printlet near-infrared (NIR) spectra, timepoint and geometric (surface area-to-volume ratio; SA/V) information, to predict in vitro dissolution profiles of dose-personalised, extended-release (ER) printlets manufactured by fused deposition modelling. Printlets varying in theophylline, hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC), and D-mannitol were produced in three distinct volumes and SA/Vs for training and three distinct volumes of equal SA/V for testing. Partial least squares (PLS) and Random Forest (RF) regression were investigated through prediction of single or multiple dependent release variables. RF models using a single response variable with features Min-Max scaled outperformed multi-response RF and PLS approaches. Further feature reduction based on spectral variance enhanced the predictive capability, with retraining using the 10 most informative features achieving good predictive performance (R2 = 0.994, RMSEtrain = 1.80%, RMSEtest = 2.75%). Time and SA/V were the most dictating features, while the retained NIR wavelengths, corresponding to characteristic vibrations from theophylline and HPC, offered model fine-tuning. The predicted dissolution profiles were equivalent to experimentally determined profiles for all test printlets, based on f1 and f2 similarity criteria. These results support the use of NIR spectroscopy with geometric parameters through multivariate modelling as a non-destructive approach for predicting drug release from 3D printed ER tablets to advance quality assurance for personalised pharmaceutical manufacturing.

articles.title: A tumor-microenvironment-responsive M1 macrophage-membrane-camouflaged nanoplatform potentiates polyphyllin VII immunotherapy through disrupting the ASNS-mTOR axis and inducing immunogenic cell death for solid tumor treatment.
articles.abstract: Polyphyllin VII, a steroidal saponin derived from Paris polyphylla, exhibits potent anti-tumor activity across multiple cancer types. Its clinical application is severely hampered by poor water solubility, non-specific biodistribution, and inherent cytotoxicity to normal tissues. Here, we report a rationally engineered biomimetic nanoplatform -M1-PVII·MSN@PDA- that systematically addresses these translational bottlenecks through a tri-functional design: mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) provide high-capacity drug loading and aqueous dispersibility; a polydopamine (PDA) coating serves as a tumor-microenvironment-responsive molecular gatekeeper, preventing premature drug leakage during systemic circulation while enabling pH/ near-infrared (NIR)-triggered release at tumor sites; and M1 macrophage membrane camouflage confers immune evasion, prolonged circulation, and active tumor homing through inherited surface proteins including CD47 and integrin α4/β1. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo characterization demonstrates that this nanoparticle achieves a high PVII loading efficiency, suppresses premature drug release in physiological conditions, and selectively releases its payload under tumor-mimicking acidic and oxidative conditions. Mechanistically, released PVII disrupts the asparagine synthetase (ASNS)-mTOR signaling axis, inducing metabolic reprogramming and asparagine depletion in tumor cells, thereby suppressing proliferation and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD) characterized by calreticulin (CRT) exposure and HMGB1 release. ICD-driven danger signals promote dendritic cell (DC) maturation, facilitate cytotoxic T-lymphocyte infiltration, and reshape the immunosuppressive TME toward an immunostimulatory phenotype. In murine solid tumor models, M1-PVII·MSN@PDA demonstrates superior tumor suppression, enhanced immune activation, and favorable biosafety profiles compared to free PVII. Collectively, this work establishes a mechanistically grounded, multi-functional nanoimmunotherapy strategy that integrates metabolic intervention with innate immune reprogramming, providing a translational framework for next-generation solid tumor treatment.

articles.title: Translational feasibility of acoustic monitoring for cumulative lung-delivered dose during routine dry powder inhaler use.
articles.abstract: Conventional inhaler monitoring based on actuation counts does not capture the inhalation profiles that determine pulmonary drug deposition, and existing in vitro metrics are not directly translatable to real-world pulmonary exposure. We report a prospective real-world evaluation of an acoustic sensing system that estimates cumulative pulmonary exposure during routine dry powder inhaler (DPI) use without modifying the inhaler. The system combines noncontact acoustic sensing, acoustic-to-flow reconstruction, and an in-vitro-derived deposition response surface model to estimate lung deposition fraction, accumulated over predefined time windows as the estimated lung-delivered dose (ELDD), an in vitro-derived surrogate of cumulative pulmonary exposure. We evaluated the system in a 24-week prospective observational study of 103 adults with asthma using Turbuhaler to evaluate system feasibility and examine associations between ELDD and subsequent changes in Asthma Control Test (ACT). The system captured 17,717 valid inhalation profiles from the cohort. The mean lung deposition fraction was 32.8 ± 10.4%, and the mean 4-week ELDD was 2,382 μg. In the association analysis (48 participants, 166 exposure-outcome intervals), higher ELDD was associated with lower odds of subsequent exploratory directional ACT decline, although the association did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.055). In a sensitivity analysis extending the exposure window to 8 weeks, the group difference reached significance (p = 0.023), consistent with the known delayed anti-inflammatory effects of inhaled corticosteroids. Continuous acoustic monitoring of DPI use in routine outpatient care was feasible over a 24-week period without inhaler modification or supervised testing. Preliminary association analyses suggested that estimated cumulative pulmonary exposure may relate to subsequent asthma control outcomes, warranting further investigation in larger confirmatory studies.

articles.title: Hastatoside ameliorates alcohol-associated liver disease, potentially involving ATF4-regulated PANoptosis signaling cascades.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the therapeutic efficacy of Hastatoside (Has) against alcohol‑associated liver disease (ALD) and characterize the molecular mechanisms underlying its hepatoprotective effects. For in vivo studies, mice were fed a Lieber‑DeCarli ethanol diet for 28 days to establish ALD models, followed by ATF4 silencing via lentiviral shRNA. In vitro experiments involved exposing HepG2 cells to Has and ethanol, followed by transfection with ATF4 siRNA. The interaction between ATF4 and the ZBP1 promoter was verified using a dual‑luciferase reporter assay. Additionally, to investigate mouse bone marrow‑derived macrophages (BMDMs) and hepatocyte crosstalk in ALD, primary hepatocytes isolated from normal mice were first exposed to conditioned media-the culture supernatants of BMDMs stimulated with LPS/ATP, and were subsequently subjected to LPS/ATP stimulation in the presence or absence of Has. Our data revealed that Has downregulated ATF4 expression as well as levels of PANoptosis‑related receptors in ALD models. Silencing of ATF4 via shRNA notably reduced ZBP1 levels and ameliorated liver injury accompanied by global PANoptosis. Hepatocyte‑specific ATF4 deficiency potentiated Has‑mediated inhibition of PANoptosis pathways. Moreover, Has suppressed pyroptosis in BMDMs, thereby mitigating inflammatory responses. Collectively, these results show that Has may alleviate ALD by modulating the ATF4‑driven PANoptosis axis. In summary, our findings highlight Has as a promising candidate for therapeutic interventions against ALD.

articles.title: Sarizotan ameliorates experimental colitis via anti-inflammatory actions and 5-HT1A receptor-mediated protection against intestinal epithelial apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Sarizotan, a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) receptor agonist, has shown efficacy in treating neurodegenerative diseases and may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In this study, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of sarizotan using a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mouse model and complementary in vitro assays. Sarizotan treatment significantly alleviated colitis symptoms, reduced inflammatory infiltration and epithelial apoptosis, and improved colonic histopathology in DSS-treated mice. In vitro, sarizotan suppressed LPS-induced pro-inflammatory mRNA expression in RAW264.7 macrophages, preserved tight junction protein expression in Caco-2 monolayers, and reduced Okadaic acid (OA)-induced apoptosis in HT-29 and Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells. Furthermore, siRNA-mediated knockdown of the 5-HT1A receptor abolished the anti-apoptotic effect of sarizotan in HT-29 cells, demonstrating that its epithelial protective effect is dependent on 5-HT1A receptor activation. Together, these findings suggest that sarizotan attenuates experimental colitis through coordinated anti-inflammatory and epithelial protective effects, with 5-HT1A receptor signaling specifically mediating its anti-apoptotic activity in intestinal epithelial cells. Given its established clinical safety profile, sarizotan may represent a promising candidate for drug repurposing in the treatment of IBD.

articles.title: FTO mediated glycolytic metabolism for papillary renal cell carcinoma immune evasion.
articles.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation is the predominant internal modification in eukaryotic mRNA, characterized by the methylation of adenosine at the nitrogen-6 position. A key m6A demethylase, the Fat Mass and Obesity-associated protein (FTO) play a significant role in metabolism. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC), particularly papillary RCC, is characterized by increased glucose uptake and a shift towards anaerobic glycolysis, commonly known as the "Warburg effect". This study investigates the role of FTO in glycolytic reprogramming and immune evasion in RCC. FTO disruption resulted in a Lactate Dehydrogenase A (LDHA) expression downregulation, followed by lactate production reduction and CD8 + T cells activation. Furthermore, FTO pharmacological inhibition by DAC51 promoted CD8 + T cell activation, also resulting in increased apoptotic activity. These findings reveal a novel role for FTO in regulating tumor metabolism and immune escape in pRCC, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Melatonin-loaded proniosomes enhance gemcitabine response in gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma: Proteomic and computational insights.
articles.abstract: Acquired resistance to gemcitabine (GEM) remains a major barrier in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) therapy. Melatonin has multi-targeted antitumor activity but is limited by rapid elimination and low oral bioavailability. We developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) and evaluated its physicochemical properties, ex vivo permeation, and antitumor activity, alone and with GEM, in a GEM-resistant CCA model. MPN was prepared by a provesicular slurry method and characterized for physicochemical properties, stability, molecular dynamics (MD), and ex vivo permeation. Efficacy and tolerability were assessed in mice bearing KKU-213BGemR xenografts, and molecular changes by tumor proteomics, mapping onto an independent human intrahepatic CCA single-cell atlas, and computational target analysis. MPN formed spherical vesicles (134.87 ± 2.45 nm; entrapment efficiency 81.39%; loading 44.29%) that retained melatonin content for six months. MD simulations supported hydrophobic interactions with Span 60/cholesterol, and ex vivo flux was approximately 15.7-fold higher than that of free melatonin. GEM + MPN-Low produced the greatest reduction in tumor growth and significantly suppressed Ki-67 expression (p < 0.0001), without altering serum ALT or creatinine. Proteomics showed lower Sonic Hedgehog abundance in GEM + MPN-treated tumors. Network pharmacology identified 28 candidate targets; docking favored MMP9 (-7.69 kcal/mol) and CDK2 (-7.21 kcal/mol), and 5 × 100-ns simulations indicated a stable complex with MMP9 but a less stable one with CDK2. These predictions were not functionally validated. Overall, MPN enhanced melatonin permeation ex vivo and was associated with an improved response to GEM in resistant CCA xenograft model, supporting further pharmacokinetic and mechanistic studies of oral delivery for biliary tract cancer.

articles.title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with MASLD: A translational study.
articles.abstract: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, potentially involving systemic metabolic dysfunction and cardiac remodeling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve metabolic dysfunction in MASLD; however, their associations with cardiovascular outcomes and effects on MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. In this translational study, we integrated a real-world TriNetX cohort of patients with MASLD and T2D with complementary experimental studies in a mouse model of MASLD. Following propensity score matching, 42,910 patients were included in each treatment group. GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite cardiovascular outcome compared with sulfonylurea therapy (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% confidence interval 0.84-0.91; P < 0.001), although this association was not statistically significant in 90-day and 180-day landmark analyses. In Western diet-fed mice, GLP-1 RA treatment improved selected indices of cardiac function and attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Although myocardial fibrosis was numerically reduced, the difference compared with vehicle-treated mice was not statistically significant (P = 0.28). Molecular analyses showed reduced expression of fibrosis- and extracellular matrix remodeling-related markers, including CTGF, TGF-β1, and vimentin. Collectively, GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the primary observational analysis, although this finding was not consistently supported by sensitivity analyses. Complementary experimental findings suggest improvements in selected cardiac functional indices and changes in fibrosis-associated molecular remodeling, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Regulatory reforms and the impact on overseas new drug accessibility in China: an analysis from 2010 to 2025.
articles.abstract: In recent years, China has undertaken a series of regulatory reforms aimed at enhancing the accessibility of overseas new drugs by mitigating marketing approval lag and expediting their inclusion in the National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL). This study conducted a retrospective analysis of overseas new drugs approved in China between 2010 and 2025, emphasizing temporal shifts in drug characteristics, regulatory efficiency, and approval lag across different reform periods. Furthermore, the study examined the reimbursement status of overseas new drugs in China, identified factors influencing their inclusion in the NRDL, and explored the China-oriented research and development (R&D) strategies adopted by their holders. Following the implementation of these reforms, the number of overseas new drug approvals increased significantly, with the cumulative total reaching 361 over the 2010-2025 study period. Simultaneously, the approval lag of overseas new drugs in China experienced a reduction, with the median duration decreasing from 1,442 to 1,188 days, using the United States as a reference. Notable improvements were observed in reimbursement access, as 213 out of 361 drugs (59.0%) were incorporated into the NRDL, and the median time for inclusion in the NRDLs was reduced from 2,297 to 743 days. However, we found that drugs approved after the reforms did not have a significantly higher likelihood of being included in the NRDL. Analyses specific to different R&D strategies indicated greater regulatory flexibility in China's acceptance of overseas clinical evidence. Notably, drugs participating in multi-regional clinical trials (MRCTs) were associated with the shortest median approval lag, measured at 737.5 days. Overall, these findings highlighted the critical importance of China's integration into global drug development initiatives and the need for enhanced coordination between regulatory and reimbursement processes.

articles.title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals cumulative rare variant burden associated with susceptibility to anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury in a Han Chinese cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (AT-DILI) complicates 2-28% of tuberculosis treatments, limiting therapy and occasionally causing acute liver failure. Inter-individual susceptibility remains incompletely explained by known genetic factors. METHODS: We performed an integrated whole-exome sequencing (WES) analysis of an AT-DILI cohort, combining common variant association analysis, rare variant burden testing at the gene and pathway levels, and exploratory genotype-phenotype analyses. A matched sub-cohort was further analyzed for cis genetic-epigenetic associations between genetic variants and DNA methylation. RESULTS: Rare variant burden analysis prioritized PTGS1 as a candidate susceptibility gene (P SKAT-O = 4.58 × 10-4, Enrichment Ratio = 3.461), with an increased burden of rare functional variants observed among AT-DILI cases. Pathway-level burden analyses further indicated enrichment of biological processes related to xenobiotic metabolism, immune regulation, and cellular stress responses, including regulated cell death. A cis genetic-epigenetic association analysis in a matched sub-cohort (n = 28) identified a nominal association at the GPR132 locus, suggesting a potential relationship between genetic variation and DNA methylation. Furthermore, genotype-phenotype analyses showed that rare variant burden in S100A2 displayed nominal positive correlations with peak alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels. CONCLUSION: These findings provide an integrated characterization of candidate rare variant signals and associated biological processes in AT-DILI. The results prioritize PTGS1 and other candidate loci for further investigation and expand our understanding of potential genetic contributors to inter-individual variability in anti-tuberculosis treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Green edible crataegi fructus-derived carbon dots ameliorate hyperlipidemia via the PPARα signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia (HL) is a lipid metabolism disorder that contributes significantly to the global burden of metabolic diseases. Hence, novel pharmacological interventions are urgently needed. Our study explored the potential mechanisms by which Crataegi Fructus Carbonisata carbon dots (CFC-CDs) act against hyperlipidemia through in vivo and in vitro experiments. METHODS: We prepared CFC-CDs and comprehensively characterized them. Subsequently, we assessed the effects of CFC-CDs on serum lipid profiles in a high-fat diet-induced rat model and used transcriptomic analysis to explore the potential mechanisms underlying their lipid-lowering effects. Additionally, we developed an in vitro model of sodium oleate (OA)-induced lipid deposition in HepG2 cells and validated it using the PPARα inhibitor GW6471. RESULTS: The CFC-CDs had an ultrasmall size ranging from 1.34 to 4.67 nm and an interplanar spacing of approximately 0.210 nm. Their surfaces contained functional groups, including-OH, C=O, and C=N. These CDs exhibited excellent biocompatibility. Animal studies demonstrated that oral treatment with CFC-CDs markedly reduced high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hyperlipidemia. Liver transcriptome analysis indicated that CFC-CDs exerted lipid-lowering effects primarily by activating the PPARα signaling pathway, suggesting that CFC-CDs have significant metabolic reprogramming capabilities. CFC-CDs also exhibited excellent lipid-lowering effects in vitro, and the PPARα inhibitor GW6471 reversed the protective effects of CFC-CDs, thereby leading to lipid accumulation. CFC-CDs may be a potential therapeutic agent for HL. CONCLUSION: The above evidence suggests that CFC-CDs synthesized by one-step calcination can significantly improve lipid metabolism disorders. Our study shows that CFC-CDs are a biomass-derived carbonaceous nanomaterial exhibiting effective lipid-lowering properties and broadening their potential clinical applications. This research provides crucial insights into the use of CFC-CDs in metabolic disease treatment and lays a solid experimental foundation for developing a new lipid-lowering candidate.

articles.title: Iron overload disrupts bone homeostasis via dual pathways: inducing ferroptosis of preosteoblastic cells and shaping a proinflammatory immune milieu.
articles.abstract: Iron overload is regarded as an independent risk factor for osteoporosis, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the impact of iron overload on bone homeostasis using a combination of in vivo and in vitro models. An iron overload rat model was established, and investigations were complemented by cellular assays utilizing mouse embryonic osteoblast precursor cells (MC3T3-E1) and macrophages. The in vivo results demonstrated that iron overload significantly reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and disrupted bone microarchitecture. These structural changes were accompanied by an enhanced inflammatory response within the bone tissue and the aberrant expression of ferroptosis markers. The in vitro experiments confirmed that iron overload induced ferroptosis and inhibited osteogenic differentiation in MC3T3-E1 cells by triggering oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. This process was closely associated with the significant upregulation of the ATPase H+ transporting V0 subunit D2 (Atp6v0d2) gene. Notably, plasmid-mediated knockdown of Atp6v0d2 substantially alleviated ferroptosis and rescued osteogenic function in iron-overloaded preosteoblastic cells. Furthermore, our study revealed that iron overload drove macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype. Conditioned medium from these polarized M1 macrophages induced apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in preosteoblastic cells while promoting osteoclast differentiation, an effect mediated by the activation of the IL-17 signaling pathway. In conclusion, this study revealed a dual mechanism by which iron overload disrupted bone homeostasis: it directly induced ferroptosis in osteogenic cells and indirectly shaped a pro-inflammatory immune microenvironment. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of iron overload-induced osteoporosis and offer a new perspective for understanding bone metabolic dysregulation under iron overload conditions.

articles.title: Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the peroxisomal biogenesis factor proteins and interferes with lipid metabolism to affect the growth of liver cancer cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary liver cancer is the sixth most commonly diagnosed cancer and the third most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Chansu is made by processing and drying the white serous fluid of the posterior ear and skin glands of Bufo bufo gargarizans Cantor or Bufo melanostictus Schneider. Chansu is a well-known traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) that is mainly used for detoxification, detumescence, analgesia, the treatment of cancer, and heart failure. Cinobufagin, as a bufadienolide, has been reported as the main antitumor active component of Chansu. However, the molecular mechanisms related to the anticancer effects of cinobufagin still remain elusive. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study is to explore whether cinobufagin inhibits the growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells by inducing peroxisome dysfunction and interfering with lipid metabolism. METHODS: The protein levels of catalase, ABCD3, PEX5, PEX6, and PEX10 in human hepatoma cells were analyzed by Western blotting. The effects of cinobufagin on the viability of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 cells were detected by cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and clone formation assay. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) transfection was used to explore whether inhibition of PEX could enhance the inhibitory effect of cinobufagin on cell growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells. The effects of cinobufagin on lipid metabolism were analyzed by untargeted metabolomics. The in vivo antitumor effects of cinobufagin were verified by animal studies. RESULTS: Cinobufagin causes peroxisome dysfunction in HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells. From a mechanistic point of view, we reveal that cinobufagin downregulates the expression of PEX5, PEX10, and PEX6. In addition, through RNA interference, cinobufagin partially blocks the growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells and restrains the expression of lipid metabolism-related proteins via downregulating the expression of PEX5 and PEX10. Subsequently, we perform a non-targeted metabolomics analysis of the cells and find that cinobufagin exerts its anti-hepatoma effects by interfering with lipid metabolic reprogramming. The results show that cinobufagin mainly interferes with glycerophospholipid and fatty acyl levels. In addition, in vivo experiments reveal that cinobufagin restrains tumor growth without obvious adverse effects. Serum metabolomics analyses reveal that cinobufagin causes significant changes in the levels of lipid and lipid-like differential metabolites. CONCLUSION: Cinobufagin is a promising natural drug for the treatment of liver cancer, and PEXs may be potential molecular targets of cinobufagin to exert anticancer effects. Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the proteins encoded by the PEX genes and interferes with lipid metabolism to restrain the growth of liver cancer cells.

articles.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential. METHODS: In the present research, the antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic properties of the ethyl acetate extract of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots were evaluated using both in vitro and in silico assessments. The crude extract was subjected to GC-MS profiling, which tentatively identified several metabolites, followed by molecular docking, drug-likeness, pharmacokinetic and toxicity prediction analyses. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The crude extract has shown broad spectrum antibacterial activity with inhibition zone of 15.66 ± 0.57 mm against Escherichia coli, 14.66 ± 1.52 mm against Staphylococcus aureus, 14.00 ± 0.00 mm against Staphylococcus epidermidis and 13.33 ± 0.57 mm against Bacillus subtilis. Minimum inhibitory concentration values were 16, 32, 64, and 64 μg/mL, while minimum bactericidal concentration values were 32, 32, 64, and 128 μg/mL, respectively. The extract showed concentration-dependent responses in chemical antioxidant assays, including DPPH radical-scavenging, hydrogen peroxide-scavenging, reducing-power and total antioxidant-capacity assays. A strong correlation between chemical antioxidant capacity and total phenolics (R2 = 0.9752-0.9986) and total flavonoids (R2 = 0.9814-0.9956) content was found. The extract exhibited concentration-dependent cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells with an IC50 value of 69.20 μg/mL that had positive correlation with the phenolics and flavonoids content. The analysis of GC-MS points to the presence of several metabolites, including 2-Buten-1-one, 1,3-diphenyl- (dypnone, a β-methyl2-Buten-1-one, 1,3-diphenyl-; CID 95329) which showed the highest binding affinity to selected protein targets, along with favourable drug-likeness, in silico pharmacokinetic and toxicity properties. The extract demonstrated antibacterial activity, measurable chemical antioxidant/ radical-scavenging properties, and cytotoxic effects under the experimental conditions. Integrated experimental and computational studies highlighted the tentatively identified 2-Buten-1-one, 1,3-diphenyl- as a compound of interest for further investigation. CONCLUSION: These findings provide preliminary indication for the possible biological activity of the Aspergillus sp. GK1 extract and support further bioassay- guided fractionation, isolation, structural characterization, mechanistic studies, and in vivo analysis of its active constituents.

articles.title: Model-informed precision dosing of vancomycin and amikacin in critically ill neonates: a pre- and post-intervention study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antimicrobial dosing in neonates is complicated by extreme developmental pharmacokinetic (PK) variability. Traditional therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) fails to achieve PK/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment in this vulnerable population. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether implementation of Bayesian model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) improved PK/PD target attainment and exposure dose adjustment compared with conventional TDM in critically ill neonates. METHODS: This pre- and post-intervention design comparing a historical retrospective cohort with a prospective MIPD validation single-center cohort study included 61 neonates receiving vancomycin or amikacin. An initial observational phase with standard dosing (n = 30) was followed by an intervention phase (n = 31) using Bayesian dose adjustment. Secondary outcomes included acute nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, infection-related inflammatory biomarkers (ΔCRP and ΔProcalcitonin), illness severity (ΔSNAPPE-II), and the treatment-duration-to-hospital-length-of-stay ratio (DOT/LOS) in NICU. RESULTS: Regarding posterior model concordance, agreement for vancomycin was limited, as evidenced by an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.47 mg/L. For amikacin, concordance was modest (overall MAE: 8.96 mg/L; median absolute error [MdAE]: 1.31 mg/L), reflecting persistent modeling challenges. For vancomycin, therapeutic target attainment was higher with MIPD than with standard dosing (5/30, 16.7% vs. 1/26, 3.8%). Similarly for amikacin, therapeutic target attainment was higher in the MIPD group (10/27, 37.0% vs. 5/26, 19.2%). In an exploratory secondary analysis, ΔSNAPPE-II differed between the standard dosing and MIPD cohorts (-2.5 vs. 0; p = 0.040), favoring standard dosing; as SNAPPE-II is not validated for longitudinal monitoring and the design was non-randomized, this does not constitute evidence of clinical benefit for either strategy. For the overall combined cohort, DOT/LOS was significantly lower in the MIPD group (p = 0.043). No differences in the rates of acute kidney injury (6.9% vs. 10.0%, p = 1.000) or ototoxicity (8.0% vs. 7.1%, p = 1.000) were detected, although the study was underpowered to rule out clinically important differences. CONCLUSION: Bayesian MIPD was associated with numerically but not statistically higher pharmacodynamic target attainment (AUC/MIC and Cmax/MIC) for vancomycin and amikacin, and no improvement in clinical outcomes was demonstrated. While amikacin modeling requires further refinement, adequately powered trials are needed to definitively assess the impact of MIPD on safety and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: MAOMAO: an ontology-guided FAIR resource for harmonized peptide toxicity data.
Esketamine alleviates the pain-depression dyad: insights from exploratory transcriptomic profiling and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations within the anterior cingulate cortex.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The molecular mechanisms driving esketamine (ESK) efficacy in the pain-depression dyad (PDD) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of a sub-anesthetic ESK regimen on cortical expression profiles and exploratory signaling markers within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). METHODS: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into Sham, PDD, and PDD + ESK groups. The PDD model, established via chronic constriction injury (CCI), was validated using a behavioral test battery tracking mechanical allodynia and depression-like phenotypes. On day 21 post-surgery, PDD + ESK rats received a single esketamine injection (15 mg/kg, i.p.). Multi-regional c-Fos expression mapping across the PFC, HPC, and ACC identified the primary responsive structure, followed by dual immunofluorescence for cellular phenotyping. Finally, ACC excitatory neuronal calcium dynamics, exploratory transcriptomic profiles, and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations (including GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation alongside synaptic markers) were evaluated using fiber photometry, RNA sequencing, and Western blotting. RESULTS: ESK alleviated pain hypersensitivity, behavioral despair, and anhedonia in PDD rats. Regional c-Fos profiling identified the ACC as the primary reactive locus, with activation localized predominantly to CaMKIIα-positive neurons. Fiber photometry confirmed that ESK attenuated functional hyperactivation in these ACC excitatory neurons. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling (unadjusted P < 0.05) revealed candidate altered transcripts, identifying Wnt4 as an exploratory molecular marker for further investigation. Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure. CONCLUSION: A single sub-anesthetic ESK dose effectively alleviates PDD behavioral phenotypes in rats. This therapeutic efficacy is associated with Wnt4-related molecular adjustments coupled with putative downstream GSK3β-mTOR signaling alterations within the ACC CaMKIIα-positive neurons, providing exploratory transcriptomic and molecular insights into cortical adaptations in pain-related affective disorders.

articles.title: Comparison of azithromycin and doxycycline for the treatment of Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia (CPP) has received increasing clinical attention worldwide in recent years. Although doxycycline is the recommended first-line therapy and macrolides serve as alternatives, no studies have directly compared their clinical efficacy in the general adult population. This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes between doxycycline and azithromycin in adult patients with CPP. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 57 adult patients with CPP at Peking University Third Hospital from 2021 to 2025, of whom 31 received doxycycline and 26 received azithromycin. Demographic characteristics, laboratory findings, and clinical outcomes were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, including comorbidities and laboratory findings, were comparable between groups. Respiratory support requirements and glucocorticoid use were similar (all P > 0.05). A numerical imbalance in Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission rate was observed, with 16.1% in the doxycycline group and 0% in the azithromycin group (P = 0.056); this difference likely reflects treatment-selection bias given the small sample size. No significant differences were observed in 28-day discharge rate (96.8% vs. 100%), mortality (3.2% vs. 0%), median length of hospital stay (6 vs. 6 days, P = 0.691), or time to defervescence (2 vs. 2 days, P = 0.436). CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences were observed in measured short-term clinical outcomes between doxycycline and azithromycin for CPP. Both may be reasonable therapeutic options, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given limited statistical power and potential confounding by indication, especially where drug availability or susceptibility data are limited.

articles.title: The Schisandra-Salvia-Hawthorn herbal formulation demonstrates therapeutic efficacy in ameliorating hyperlipidemia.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study investigates the potential efficacy and action mechanism of a herbal formulation comprising Schisandra chinensis, Salvia miltiorrhiza and Hawthorn (SSH) in the treatment of hyperlipidemia. METHODS: A hyperlipidemic cell model was established by free fatty acid (FFA)-induced HepG2 cells and a hyperlipidemic mouse model was established by high-fat diet (HFD)-induced C57BL/6 mice. Cell viability of HepG2 cells was assessed by MTT assay. Serum lipid profiles (TC, TG, LDL-C, HDL-C) were quantified via the corresponding kits. Hepatic tissue pathology was evaluated via Oil Red O staining and HE staining. Serum inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6) were measured through ELISA. The mRNA and protein expression of seven key targets (APOB, LDLR, OLR1, PPARG, PRKCA, RXRA, NCF1) identified via network pharmacology prediction, were detected using qRT-PCR and Western blot. Besides, protein levels of p-p65 and p65 were detected by Western blot. Immunofluorescence staining was used to monitor p65 subcellular distribution, and DCFH-DA-based fluorescence detection was conducted to assess ROS production. RESULTS: In FFA-induced HepG2 cells, TC, TG, and lipid accumulation were reduced after SSH treatment. In HFD-induced mice, SSH treatment attenuated HFD-induced increases in serum TC, TG, and LDL-C levels, while elevating the level of HDL-C. It also reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, hepatic injury and expression of TNF-α and IL-6. Mechanistically, SSH formulation reversed HFD-driven dysregulation of the predicted targets: it downregulated the expression of APOB, OLR1, PRKCA, RXRA, PPARG and NCF1, and upregulated the expression of LDLR. FFA caused increases of OLR1 protein expression, PRKCA protein expression and phosphorylation of NF-κB p65 as well as ROS production in HepG2 cells, which were reversed by SSH treatment. CONCLUSION: The SSH formulation mitigated hyperlipidemia by restoring lipid homeostasis and suppressing inflammation. Its efficacy was mediated through a multi-target mechanism, coordinately regulating lipoprotein metabolism (APOB/LDLR), oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling (OLR1/PRKCA/NCF1), and nuclear receptor activity (PPARG/RXRA).

articles.title: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes following exposure to GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists: a time-window-stratified systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes after preconception or gestational exposure to glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual glucagon-like peptide-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists, and to assess the reproducibility of reported safety signals. METHODS: Six databases plus a drug-level safety search were searched through 16 July 2026. Exposure was classified into four clinically defined time windows. Independent studies or data sources were the analytic unit; one primary comparator was selected per study, and odds ratios and risk ratios were synthesized separately. Random-effects meta-analysis, timing-stratified and dominant-study sensitivity analyses, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment, and GRADE certainty assessment were used. RESULTS: Fourteen comparative data sources were included; 13 were quantitatively eligible and eight contributed to at least one pooled estimate. In the timing-specific analysis of major congenital malformations, four studies with verified periconceptional/first-trimester exposure yielded an odds ratio of 0.99 (95% confidence interval 0.77-1.27). A secondary pregnancy-period analysis that added one unadjusted, trimester-unspecified cohort yielded 1.00 (0.94-1.06); that cohort contributed 93.5% of the weight. Pooled preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, and stillbirth analyses showed no statistically significant differences. Preeclampsia and other sparse outcomes were not pooled. Certainty was very low for all key outcomes. CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear or consistent increase in major congenital malformation risk, but very low certainty, imprecision, residual confounding, heterogeneous comparators, sparse agent-specific data, and uncertain exposure timing preclude conclusions of safety. Reported preeclampsia and renal or urinary signals have not been independently replicated.

articles.title: Benzoylaconine suppresses colorectal cancer progression by modulating the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) has a high incidence, and both metastasis and drug resistance remain formidable challenges in clinical management. Owing to their multi-target activity and favorable safety profiles, natural products have become a prolific source for anticancer drug discovery. Benzoylaconine (BAC) is a secondary metabolite of aconitine with markedly attenuated toxicity that retains anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antitumor properties; however, its antitumor effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms in CRC are poorly defined. This study was designed to systematically characterize the impact of BAC on the malignant phenotypes of CRC cells and to identify its potential molecular targets. METHODS: HCT116 and SW480 cells were used as model systems. Proliferation was assessed by MTT and EdU assays; migration and invasion by wound-healing and Transwell assays, respectively; cell cycle and apoptosis by flow cytometry. Network pharmacology was applied to predict core targets and construct a protein-protein interaction network. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations examined binding; SPR verified direct binding to CDK2 and MMP2. RNA-seq identified differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. Western blotting validated key protein changes. Patient-derived CRC organoids (PDOs) were established to evaluate BAC efficacy; organoid viability was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® 2.0 assay, and morphology by bright-field microscopy. RESULTS: BAC dose- and time-dependently inhibited CRC cell proliferation and EdU positivity, slowed wound closure, and reduced Transwell invasion, indicating impaired migration and invasion. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that BAC induced G1/S cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Network pharmacology identified CDK2 and MMP2 as key targets; molecular dynamics and SPR confirmed stable binding (KD ≈ 3.9 and 4.4 μM). RNA-seq showed enrichment of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and tumor invasion. Western blotting revealed that BAC dose-dependently downregulated CDK2, CDK6, MMP2, Cyclin E1, and Cyclin D1, and upregulated p21. BAC also inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer organoids. CONCLUSION: BAC induces G1/S cell cycle arrest in CRC cells, likely through modulation of the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis, thereby suppressing proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis, and may represent a promising lead for CRC therapy.

articles.title: Trans-anethole attenuates streptozotocin-induced cognitive dysfunction by modulating oxidative stress and cholinergic activity.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cognitive impairment is a neurological disorder defined as an inability to learn, think, judge, remember, and make decisions. The primary cause of chronic, age- related cognitive decline is Alzheimer's disease (AD), which is frequently studied as a representative model. The current therapies for AD provide only symptomatic relief, which necessitates the need for safer, multi-target treatments. Trans- anethole, the primary constituent of Illicium verum, Pimpinella anisum, and Foeniculum vulgare, is an aromatic molecule that possesses several pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which may have neuroprotective benefits. METHODS: The current study integrated in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches to examine the neuroprotective potential of trans- anethole. In silico studies were carried out to find out the potential molecular targets and pathways associated with the effects of trans-anethole against AD- related cognitive dysfunction. Cytotoxicity, antioxidant activity, and cholinesterase inhibition were assessed in vitro on BV2 cells. Intracerebroventricular (ICV) administration of streptozotocin (STZ: 3 mg/kg) in rats induces an insulin-resistant brain state leading to progressive cognitive and memory impairment, a condition that closely relates to sporadic Alzheimer's disease. ICV-STZ-induced Wistar rats were used to assess the effect of trans- anethole on AD-related cognitive dysfunction through behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological assessments. RESULTS: A total of 174 common targets were identified, enriching pathways including apoptosis, AGE-RAGE, TNF, and PI3K- Akt signaling. Stable interactions were observed in molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Trans-anethole demonstrates moderate cholinesterase inhibition and antioxidant activity in BV2 cells. Comparing STZ- treated rats to disease control, trans-anethole at doses of 100 mg/kg and 400 mg/kg significantly reduced lipid peroxidation, restored antioxidant enzyme levels, and attenuated cholinergic dysfunction. Histopathological findings showed qualitative preservation of hippocampal neuronal morphology. DISCUSSION: Overall, these findings suggest that trans-anethole may represent a potential neuroprotective preclinical candidate for further investigation in Alzheimer's disease-related cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and pharmacovigilance signals of immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated cystitis and ureteritis: analysis of FAERS reports and published cases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated cystitis and ureteritis are uncommon urinary immune-related adverse events that are difficult to distinguish from infection or other urinary tract complications. Their clinical phenotype and pharmacovigilance signal remain incompletely defined. METHODS: We combined a pooled analysis of published cases with a FAERS disproportionality analysis from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Published cases were reviewed for clinical presentation, treatment, rechallenge, and time-to-onset. FAERS reports were deduplicated at the CASEID level. A broad cystitis-inclusive definition included IMMUNE-MEDIATED CYSTITIS, CYSTITIS NONINFECTIVE, URETERITIS, and CYSTITIS; a high-specificity definition excluded the nonspecific Preferred Term CYSTITIS. Disproportionality was assessed using reporting odds ratios (RORs), proportional reporting ratios, chi-square statistics, and information components. RESULTS: Twenty-eight reports comprising 45 unique patients were included. The median age was 56 years, and lung cancer was the most common malignancy.
