Published cases commonly showed urinary frequency, dysuria, hematuria, leukocyturia, inflammatory imaging or cystoscopic abnormalities, and corticosteroid responsiveness. Upper urinary tract involvement was documented in 13 of 33 patients with available CT data. Median time-to-onset was 62 days among 24 evaluable cases, and recurrence occurred in 5 of 9 rechallenged patients. In FAERS, 20,257,224 deduplicated CASEIDs were analyzed. The broad cystitis-inclusive definition identified 397 ICI-associated cases and showed only a weak signal (ROR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.02-1.24), whereas the high-specificity definition identified 151 cases and yielded a stronger signal (ROR, 9.04; 95% CI, 7.63-10.70). Class-level signals were also observed, and the overall high-specificity signal remained positive across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: These findings support ICI-associated cystitis and ureteritis as an uncommon urothelial inflammatory irAE spectrum. Phenotype-aware outcome definition is important in pharmacovigilance because nonspecific cystitis coding may dilute the reporting signal.

articles.title: Hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects of Arctium lappa root extract in valproic acid-induced toxicity: biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analysis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Valproic acid (VPA) is a widely used antiepileptic drug; however, its clinical use is limited by hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis, primarily mediated through oxidative stress and inflammation. Arctium lappa root extract (ALRE) has been reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties that may confer protection against VPA-induced organ toxicity. METHODS: Phytochemical profiling of ALRE was performed using GC-MS and HPLC. In vitro cytotoxic effects were assessed in Hep3B and PANC-1 cancer cell lines, while safety was assessed in THLE-2 normal hepatic epithelial cells and H6C7 normal pancreatic ductal epithelial cells using the MTT assay. The hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects were investigated in VPA-induced toxicity in male Wistar albino rats through biochemical, oxidative stress, and histopathological analyses. RESULTS: ALRE exhibited low cytotoxicity towards THLE-2 and H6C7 cells, with IC50 values of 1,084.92 and 1,174.62 μg/mL, respectively. VPA administration markedly increased serum levels of ALT (127.67 ± 4.34 U/L), AST (153.67 ± 4.91 U/L), ALP (178.67 ± 5.21 U/L), GGT (7.67 ± 0.09 U/L), amylase (47.33 ± 2.91 U/L), and lipase (49.00 ± 3.79 U/L) compared with the control group (p < 0.05). These enzyme levels were considerably lowered by ALRE administration, especially at 500 mg/kg. Furthermore, ALRE restored antioxidant defences (SOD, CAT, and GSH), malondialdehyde levels were decreased, and the histological architecture of the liver and pancreas was improved. CONCLUSION: ALRE effectively attenuated VPA-induced hepatic and pancreatic injury through antioxidant and cytoprotective mechanisms while exhibiting minimal toxicity towards normal hepatic and pancreatic cells. These findings support the potential therapeutic application of A. lappa as a natural protective against VPA-associated hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis. Further studies are warranted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and pharmacokinetic interactions underlying the protective effects of ALRE.

articles.title: Rutin interferes with hnRNP L phase separation and modulates the PKM2-lactate-H3K9la axis in pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis is a chronic and progressive lung disease with limited treatment options; it is urgent to develop new drugs. PURPOSE: This study investigated the anti-pulmonary fibrosis effects and mechanism of rutin, and sought to provide a potential lead compound for further development of anti-pulmonary fibrosis agents. METHODS: The anti-pulmonary fibrosis effect of rutin was assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), real-time cell proliferation analysis and scratch wound healing assay in Transforming Growth Factor-β1(TGF-β1)-stimulated Medical Research Council cell strain-5 (MRC-5) cells, along with lung function tests, MicroCT imaging, Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) and Masson staining in mice with induced pulmonary fibrosis. The mechanism of rutin was explored through molecular docking, the surface plasmon resonance assay, the cell thermal shift assay (CETSA), droplet formation observation, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, transcriptome sequencing, Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA), Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and Chromatin Immunoprecipitation-Polymerase Chain Reaction (ChIP-PCR). RESULTS: Rutin inhibited fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation, myofibroblast proliferation and migration, and extracellular matrix deposition. Moreover, rutin effectively improved lung function, including forced vital capacity, dynamic lung compliance and total lung capacity. Additionally, rutin markedly alleviated fibrotic features, such as honeycomb lung reduction, preserved alveolar structure and thinned alveolar walls. Mechanistically, our data support a model in which rutin may interfere with hnRNP L phase separation, and this interference is associated with reduced PKM2 generation, decreased lactate production and subsequent loss of H3K9la. The reduced H3K9la, in turn, correlated with suppressed PKM2 transcription, suggesting a self-limiting regulatory circuit. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that rutin may interfere with the regulatory interplay involving hnRNP L phase separation, PKM2 alternative splicing, lactate, and H3K9la, which is associated with the attenuation of pulmonary fibrosis. While these data reveal a potential mechanistic framework, definitive causality at each step of this regulatory axis remains to be established. Further studies are warranted to validate this model and to optimize the bioavailability of rutin for therapeutic application.

articles.title: Community Pharmacists' Perspectives and Experiences of Deprescribing in Québec, Canada: Findings From a Survey.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Community pharmacists in Quebec can bill for deprescribing. However, uptake remains low. We aimed to explore how community pharmacists perceive and engage in deprescribing. METHODS: Community pharmacists were invited to complete an online survey through a pharmacists' social media group and a newsletter. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and univariate chi-square tests. RESULTS: Among 366 respondents, most were women (n = 269; 74%), worked full-time (n = 282; 77%), had time for clinical interventions (n = 223; 61%), while 53% (n = 193) had fewer than 11 years of experience. Three quarters (n = 271) reported initiating deprescribing at least monthly. Side effects (n = 273; 75%) and patients' requests (n = 220; 60%) were more common reasons for deprescribing. More than 70% (n = 268) reported that prescribers usually accepted recommendations. Initial and follow-up consultations were systematically billed by 50% (n = 183) and 48% (n = 174) of respondents, respectively. Deprescribing interventions and billing practices were more common among pharmacists with dedicated clinical time and those working full time (all p < 0.01). Main barriers to billing were insufficient training (n = 217; 59%), uncertainty about reimbursement eligibility (n = 127; 35%) and lack of time (n = 112; 31%). Integrated software was the most common facilitator (n = 246; 67%). CONCLUSION: Deprescribing was commonly reported among respondents and was often prompted by clinical concerns and patient requests. Billing uncertainties and time constraints remained important barriers, highlighting opportunities to better support deprescribing in community pharmacy.

articles.title: Concomitant calcium supplementation does not compromise immunosuppressive dosing in kidney transplant recipients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Polypharmacy following kidney transplantation entails a risk of both drug-drug interactions (DDIs) and reduced patient adherence. Co-administration of calcium supplementation and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) has previously been shown to influence pharmacokinetics (PK) of MMF. In current DDI databases, there is a recommendation for 2- to 3-h time-shifted administration. Whether a similar interaction potentially exists for tacrolimus has not been evaluated. We aimed to investigate the potential PK DDI between co-administrated calcium/vitamin D supplementation and the immunosuppressive drugs MMF and tacrolimus, using volumetric absorptive microsampling (VAMS). METHODS: Twenty-five kidney transplant recipients on stable MMF, tacrolimus and prednisolone treatment provided two 12-h PK investigations of simultaneous assessment of both mycophenolic acid (MPA) and tacrolimus concentrations. One PK investigation with and one without concomitant treatment with a calcium/vitamin D supplement. Capillary blood samples using VAMS were utilized to obtain samples in a patient friendly manner. Clinically relevant interactions were assessed by the with/without ratio of AUC0-12 and Cmax in accordance with EMA bioequivalence guidelines. RESULTS: The MPA AUC0-12 ratio was 0.94 (90% confidence interval [CI], 0.83-1.07) and the Cmax ratio was 0.79 (90% CI, 0.65-0.97). For tacrolimus, the AUC0-12 and Cmax ratios were 1.00 (90% CI, 0.92-1.09) and 0.96 (90% CI, 0.87-1.07), respectively. CONCLUSION: In kidney transplant recipients there is no clinically relevant PK DDI caused by concomitant administration of calcium/vitamin D supplementation with MMF and tacrolimus. Based on these observations, recommendation of time-shifted administration of calcium supplements and immunosuppressive drugs seems unnecessary.

articles.title: Dosing HIV integrase inhibitors with enzyme inducers: Convenience vs. control?
Tenofovir diphosphate intracellular concentration following tenofovir alafenamide administration in bictegravir-containing vs. dolutegravir-containing antiretroviral regimens.
articles.abstract: This study investigates intracellular (IC) exposure of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) and its clinical determinants in experienced people living with HIV. We conducted a monocentric retrospective analysis of 86 adults treated with either bictegravir (BIC)- or dolutegravir (DTG)-containing regimen. Plasma and IC trough concentrations (Ctrough) of tenofovir diphosphate (TFV-DP) were examined in relation to demographic and renal parameters. A significant correlation emerged between plasma and IC TFV-DP Ctrough. Higher plasma TFV levels were associated with older age and reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate. Adherence calculated as proportion of days covered (PDC) did not differ between regimens. These findings provide novel real-world insights into IC TFV-DP pharmacokinetics and suggest that BIC-containing regimens may enhance IC drug accumulation, although the impact of this observation on virological outcomes requires further studies.

articles.title: Comparative treatment effects of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation in clinical practice vary over time due to channelling.
articles.abstract: AIM: Temporal shifts in patient characteristics can influence comparative treatment effects within a certain indication. We investigated patient characteristics and comparative effectiveness and safety for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and warfarin over the time period where DOACs replaced warfarin as preferred stroke prophylaxis in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). METHODS: We applied the cohort design to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and created 12 sequential subcohorts of patients with NVAF between 2011 and 2023. Patients with a DOAC or warfarin prescription following a 1-year prescription-free period were included. Baseline characteristics were compared between subcohorts. Survival analysis was used to evaluate the risk of ischaemic stroke (effectiveness outcome) and major bleeds (safety outcome). RESULTS: We included 207 393 patients with NVAF (45% women, 77% DOAC users, mean age 76 years). In early subcohorts, a history of stroke/transient ischaemic attack was more common among DOAC users. In later subcohorts, diabetes, deep venous thrombosis/pulmonary embolism and antihypertensive use were more common among warfarin users. History of other cardiovascular disease, renal failure and diuretic use were consistently higher among warfarin users. Over time, the crude stroke hazard ratio for DOAC users compared with warfarin users shifted from 2.66 (95% CI 2.00-3.52) to 0.62 (0.23-1.67). This trend was attenuated in adjusted analyses. No such trends were seen for major bleeds. CONCLUSION: DOACs had unfavourable effectiveness estimates in earlier subcohorts, potentially due to preferential prescribing to higher risk patients. Early observational studies may encounter initial biases, underscoring the need for robust methodological approaches when evaluating newly introduced medicines.

articles.title: Development of a novel next-generation multi-epitope vaccine targeting the Guaroa virus glycoprotein precursor through reverse vaccinology.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Guaroa virus using integrated immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology approaches. The viral glycoprotein precursor was selected as the target for epitope screening. Potential B-cell and T-cell epitopes with predicted antigenic properties, non-allergenicity, and non-toxicity were identified through computational analyses. Global population coverage assessment predicted a population coverage of 99.09% based on the selected HLA-associated epitopes. Selected epitopes were assembled into a chimeric vaccine construct containing β-defensin-3 adjuvant and linker sequences. Physicochemical analysis predicted properties relevant to solubility and recombinant expression, although these characteristics require experimental assessment. Structural prediction and refinement yielded a model in which 99.5% of residues were located within favored regions. Molecular docking predicted interactions between the vaccine construct and immune receptors TLR2, TLR3, and TLR4, with TLR4 showing the lowest docking score among the three receptors. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to assess the predicted structural behavior of the vaccine-receptor complexes. The vaccine-TLR4 complex yielded a docking score of -1212.9, while MM-GBSA analysis produced a ΔG_bind estimate of -227.14 kcal/mol based on the final trajectory frame. Immune simulation predicted increases in antibody production, cytokine release, and memory cell formation. Collectively, these findings support the computational prioritization of the construct as a vaccine candidate for further experimental investigation, although experimental and clinical validation remain necessary.

articles.title: Empirical linezolid target attainment in critically ill patients: integrating local susceptibility data and dosing strategies.
articles.abstract: Linezolid is important for treating infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria resistant to first-line agents. Severe infections often require empirical therapy before pathogen identification and susceptibility testing. This evaluation aims to compare different empirical linezolid dosing strategies in intensive care unit (ICU) patients to improve pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic target attainment while minimising toxicities. Three dosing strategies were compared: (i) standard dosing, (ii) therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)-guided dosing, and (iii) a theoretical model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) strategy based on Bayesian forecasting with a population pharmacokinetic model. Each scenario was combined with an ICU-specific minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) distribution comprising more than 19,000 isolates collected over 10 years. Data from 117 critically ill patients with 2184 TDM samples were available. Linezolid resistance was highest in ICU isolates (9.6%) compared with isolates from the intermediate care unit (4.3%), general wards (3.6%), and emergency room (1.6%). Among ICU isolates, resistance increased significantly over the 10-year study period, from 6.3% in 2015 to 11.4% in 2024. Empirical target attainment was 36.6% with standard dosing and 48.5% with TDM-guided dose adaptation, in two different ICU cohorts that showed 35.9% and 59.4% baseline target attainment, respectively. Theoretical MIPD projected target attainment in 71.4-81.6% of patients. After excluding resistant isolates, the corresponding values were 40.5%, 53.7%, and 79.0-90.3%, respectively. Integrating a large contemporary ICU-specific MIC distribution with patient-level pharmacokinetic data, our results suggest MIPD may represent a promising strategy improving target attainment, in contrast to standard regimens and TDM-guided dosing which failed to achieve adequate target exposure in ICU patients.

articles.title: Differential behavioral effects of systemic oxytocin receptor blockade across social tasks and hierarchical ranks in male mice.
articles.abstract: Oxytocin receptor signaling has been implicated in diverse social behaviors, but whether its behavioral effects depend on social tasks and an individual's position within a hierarchy remains unclear. We examined the effects of systemic administration of L-368,899, a blood-brain barrier-penetrating oxytocin receptor antagonist, across four domains of social behavior in male C57BL/6 J mice: social rank, sex preference, general social preference, and dyadic interaction. Following the establishment of stable hierarchies in the tube test, administration of L-368,899 (10 mg/kg, intraperitoneally) to first-ranked mice did not alter their hierarchical position. Rank fluctuations were observed more frequently when the antagonist was administered to second-ranked mice. In both rank conditions, the remaining cage mates received saline. In the sex-preference task, saline-treated males spent more time in the female stimulus zone than in the male stimulus zone, whereas this preference was not statistically detectable following treatment with L-368,899 (3 or 10 mg/kg). In contrast, L-368,899 did not significantly alter proximity-based preference for a novel male over a nonsocial object or affect contact duration and inter-individual distance during dyadic interactions between familiar male cage mates, in which both members of each pair received the same treatment. Thus, systemic oxytocin receptor blockade did not produce a generalized reduction in social approach. Instead, the observed behavioral patterns suggest that its effects depend on specific social behavioral tasks and hierarchical position. These findings provide a pharmacological basis for further investigation of the task- and rank-dependent contributions of oxytocin receptor signaling to social behavior.
